title: Four letters, then a long warning. Stop and listen.
subtitle: Letters whose meaning is with Allah
then: This surah came near the end of the Prophet's ﷺ years in Makkah. He had called his people for a long time, and {trap}most had turned a deaf ear.{/trap} The surah opens with four letters whose meaning is {idea}known to Allah{/idea}, before a long message to people who had stopped listening.
now: You open the app on the bus, thumb already on the scroll bar. Four letters you cannot explain sit at the top. {idea}You do not have to decode them. You only have to slow down.{/idea}
old: If I cannot understand something right away, I move past it.
new: Some words are there to stop me and make me ready to listen.
try: Before you read your next page of Quran, sit still for ten seconds first.

title: Do not let the message feel heavy in your chest.
subtitle: Carrying a truth others do not want
then: The Prophet ﷺ faced a city that mocked him. Scholars explained the tightness here as doubt, or {trap}hesitation to deliver it{/trap}. The tafsir links it to {idea}being patient like the messengers of strong will{/idea}.
now: Your cousins are arguing in the family group chat, and you know something true that would help. You type it, delete it, type it again. {trap}What will they think of me?{/trap} {reward}The truth does not need you to be embarrassed for it.{/reward}
old: If people may not like what is right, I should keep quiet.
new: What comes from Allah does not need me to feel cramped about it.
try: Say one kind, true thing today that you have been holding back.

title: Follow what your Lord sent, not other guides.
subtitle: Who you take your direction from
then: This verse speaks to everyone, not only the Prophet ﷺ. The tafsir explains: {idea}follow the Book he brought{/idea}, and do not leave it to follow someone else's judgment. It ties this to verses saying that {trap}following most people on earth leads astray{/trap}.
now: A big decision at work, and you check what your favorite influencer says, then what everyone in the comments thinks. {trap}A thousand likes feel like proof.{/trap} {idea}Ask first what your Lord has already said.{/idea}
old: If lots of people follow it, it is probably fine.
new: The number of followers does not make a guide right.
try: For one choice today, ask yourself what Allah would want before you check anyone else.

title: It came while they slept, at night or at noon.
subtitle: Towns caught in their moments of rest
then: The people of Makkah were being reminded of towns before them. The tafsir says they were destroyed {trap}for defying and rejecting their messengers{/trap}. It came at night or at the noon nap, {idea}times of rest and heedlessness{/idea}.
now: Sunday afternoon. Couch, phone, nowhere to be. The thought that you should fix things with Allah drifts by, and you think, {trap}later, there is plenty of time{/trap}. {idea}Nobody gets a warning before their last ordinary afternoon.{/idea}
old: Change can wait until life is less busy.
new: My quiet, careless hours are exactly when I should not feel safe.
try: Pick one thing you keep saying you will start later, and do two minutes of it today.

title: Their only words at the end: we were wrong.
subtitle: An admission that came too late
then: The towns of the last verse had no clever excuse when the end came. The tafsir says {trap}they admitted their sins and that they deserved it{/trap}. {idea}The truth they had denied came out of their own mouths.{/idea}
now: The argument with your spouse that went on for weeks. Deep down you knew you were wrong on day one. You will say it eventually anyway. {reward}Saying it now is the version that still repairs something.{/reward}
old: I will admit my mistake when I have no other choice.
new: An admission is worth most before I am forced to make it.
try: Say "I was wrong about that" to one person, or to Allah in your prayer, today.

title: Both will be asked: the messengers and their listeners.
subtitle: Two questions on the Day
then: The tafsir explains that Allah will ask the nations {idea}how they responded to His messengers{/idea}. He will also ask the messengers if they delivered it. Ibn Abbas said the messengers are asked {reward}about what they conveyed{/reward}.
now: You heard a talk last month that hit you hard. You nodded, shared the clip, and moved on. {idea}One day the question will not be whether it was said. It will be what you did after hearing it.{/idea}
old: Hearing good advice is the same as having done something.
new: Every message I hear comes with a question about my answer.
try: Recall one reminder you heard this week and act on one small piece of it.

title: He was never absent. He will tell the whole story.
subtitle: A full record, told with knowledge
then: Ibn Abbas said {idea}the Book will be brought out and it will speak{/idea}, showing what people did. The tafsir adds that Allah {trap}misses nothing, big or small{/trap}. It quotes the verse that not a leaf falls without His knowing.
now: The late night at your desk when nobody saw you finish someone else's work for them. The message you deleted before anyone read it. {idea}He was there for both.{/idea} {reward}The good you thought went unseen was seen too.{/reward}
old: What no one saw does not really count.
new: Allah was present for all of it, the hidden good and the hidden bad.
try: Do one good thing today that no one else will ever know about.

title: The scale that Day is true. Heavy means success.
subtitle: A weighing that wrongs no one
then: The tafsir says the weighing is true because {idea}Allah will not wrong anyone{/idea}. It tells the hadith of a man with ninety-nine scrolls of sins and {reward}one card with La ilaha illallah that outweighed them{/reward}. It also tells how the Prophet ﷺ said Ibn Mas'ud's thin legs were heavier on the scale than Mount Uhud.
now: You compare yourself to the colleague with the bigger title and the bigger house. You feel light. {reward}The scale does not weigh what the office notices. It weighs sincerity.{/reward}
old: People who look important must weigh more with Allah.
new: Real weight is what is true in my heart and deeds, not how big I look.
try: Say La ilaha illallah slowly three times today and mean every word.

title: A light scale means you lost yourself.
subtitle: The loss that comes from ignoring the signs

row.title: themselves
sub: the loss of one's own soul

then: Next to the heavy scale, the verse gives the light one. The tafsir links it to verses where {trap}those with light scales lose themselves{/trap}. The reason in this verse is how they {trap}treated Allah's signs unjustly{/trap}.
now: You lose a wallet and you search every pocket. You lose a habit of prayer and barely notice. {idea}The verse puts the real loss somewhere you were not looking: in your own self.{/idea}
old: Losing money is the worst kind of loss.
new: The worst loss is losing myself by brushing off what Allah shows me.
try: Think of one reminder you keep dismissing, and give it five honest minutes today.

title: He settled you on earth and gave you a living.
subtitle: Gifts that are easy to forget
then: After the warnings, the surah turns to gifts. The tafsir lists {reward}a stable earth, mountains, rivers, homes, rain, trade and professions{/reward}. {trap}Yet most give little thanks.{/trap}
now: Payday. The money lands and in the same minute it is gone in your head: rent, bills, the thing you want. {reward}The job, the health to do it, the road to get there.{/reward} You forgot to say thank you for any of it.
old: I worked for my salary, so it is simply mine.
new: Even my ability to earn was set up for me by Allah.
try: On your next payday or purchase, say alhamdulillah before you spend.

title: Honored at the start, with an enemy watching.
subtitle: Adam's honor and the one who refused

key.label: Why this is told to me

row.title: you
sub: the honor and the enemy are yours

then: The verse says {idea}We created you{/idea}, speaking of Adam to all his children. The tafsir says Allah tells us of {reward}our father's honor{/reward} and of {trap}Shaytan's envy, which still continues{/trap}, so we take care not to follow him.
now: You feel worthless after a bad review at work, or a cruel comment online. {reward}Your father was honored by the angels.{/reward} {trap}The one who hated him still wants you to feel small and to stay small.{/trap}
old: I am nothing special.
new: I come from an honored father, and I have a real enemy who envies that.
try: When you hear a voice today calling you worthless, answer it with a'udhu billah.

title: I am better than him. The first proud excuse.
subtitle: Comparing origins instead of obeying
then: Allah asked Iblis what stopped him. Ibn Kathir says {trap}his excuse was worse than the crime itself{/trap}. He looked at what Adam was made of and not at the honor Allah gave him. The tafsir adds that {idea}clay grows and nourishes, while fire burns and rushes{/idea}.
now: A new hire is promoted over you. Your first thought: {trap}I have been here longer, I studied more, I am better than him{/trap}. {idea}The comparison feels like logic. It is the oldest kind of pride.{/idea}
old: I am better than them, so the rules should not apply to me.
new: "I am better than him" is the first excuse pride ever used.
try: Catch one moment today where you think "I am better than" someone, and pray for them instead.

title: He wanted to rise and was made low.
subtitle: Pride receives its opposite

picture.label: What he wanted, what he got

then: Allah told Iblis that {trap}arrogance has no place there{/trap}. The tafsir says he was made humiliated as a fitting result of his intention, {idea}given the opposite of what he wanted{/idea}.
now: You refuse to apologize in the meeting because it would look weak. A month later the whole team quietly avoids you. {idea}The pride that was meant to keep you high is what brought you down.{/idea}
old: If I back down, I lose respect.
new: Pride ends up giving me the very smallness I was trying to avoid.
try: Let someone else be right in one small disagreement today.

title: He asked for time, not forgiveness.
subtitle: What Iblis did with his last request

key.label: Two ways to answer a fall

then: Just thrown out, Iblis made one request. {trap}He did not ask to be forgiven. He asked for time{/trap} until the Day people are raised. The tafsir contrasts him with Adam, whose nature led him to {reward}return to Allah, admit his error, and ask forgiveness{/reward}.
now: You got caught: a lie, a shortcut, a harsh word. You can ask for room to keep doing it more carefully. {reward}Or you can ask for forgiveness and change.{/reward} {idea}Both are requests. Only one goes somewhere good.{/idea}
old: When I get caught, I just need to be more careful next time.
new: After a fall, the question is whether I ask for time or for forgiveness.
try: Turn one mistake from this week into a sincere istighfar tonight.

title: He was given time. So the test is real.
subtitle: Why the enemy is still around
then: Allah granted what Iblis asked. The tafsir says this was {idea}out of His wisdom, His decision and decree, which none can resist{/idea}. So the enemy who refused to bow {trap}is still here, until the Day of Resurrection{/trap}.
now: The pull to scroll instead of pray. The whisper to say the harsh thing in the group chat. {trap}It is not random.{/trap} {idea}Knowing the enemy was given time is what makes you careful with yours.{/idea}
old: Bad urges are just random moods.
new: There is an enemy who was given time, so I use mine on purpose.
try: Notice one whisper today that pulls you away from good, and name it as his.

title: He blamed Allah, then sat down on the straight path.
subtitle: Where the enemy chose to wait
then: Given his respite, Iblis went on in defiance. He {trap}blamed Allah for his own error{/trap}, then promised to wait on the straight path. The tafsir quotes a hadith that {trap}Shaytan sat on every path of the son of Adam{/trap}: Islam, hijrah, striving. {reward}Each time the man disobeyed him and kept going.{/reward}
now: You finally sign up for the Quran class. That same night: {trap}you are too busy, you will quit anyway, who do you think you are?{/trap} {idea}The resistance shows up right on the road you chose.{/idea}
old: If doing good feels hard, maybe it is not meant for me.
new: The pushback on a good path is a sign of the one who waits there.
try: Pick the good thing you have been talked out of, and take one step on it today.

title: From the front, back, right and left. Not from above.
subtitle: Four directions of attack

picture.label: Ibn Abbas on the four sides

then: Ibn Abbas explained each side: {trap}doubts about the Hereafter, love of this world, confusion in religion, temptation to sin{/trap}. He also noted Iblis did not say from above, {reward}because mercy comes down from above{/reward}. The tafsir mentions the Prophet's ﷺ morning and evening dua asking protection from every side.
now: Some days it feels like it comes from everywhere. The doubt at 2am, the shopping app, the argument about religion online, the private temptation. {reward}Look up. That side was never his.{/reward}
old: I am surrounded and there is no way out of this.
new: Every side can be attacked except the one mercy comes from.
try: Tonight, ask Allah to protect you from in front, behind, right, left and above.

title: Driven out, despised, and his followers go with him.
subtitle: Following him means sharing his end
then: Scholars explained the words as {trap}despised, belittled, banished{/trap}. Those who follow him meet the same end. The tafsir links it to a verse where Allah tells him that {reward}over My servants you have no authority{/reward}.
now: You see a friend copy the way someone talks and acts until they are the same person. Following is how you end up where someone else is going. {reward}His pull is real, but he cannot make you follow.{/reward}
old: I am just going along with it, it is not really my choice.
new: Following is a choice, and I end up where the one I follow ends up.
try: Ask yourself honestly whose habits you have been copying lately.

title: Eat from everywhere. Just not this one tree.
subtitle: A whole garden open, one line drawn

row.title: a garden, minus one tree
sub: almost all of it is open

then: Allah let Adam and his wife live in Paradise and {reward}eat from all its fruits{/reward}. Only {trap}one tree{/trap} was off limits. The tafsir says Shaytan envied them and started to plot.
now: You fixate on the one thing you are told no to, and forget the hundred things you are free to enjoy. {reward}Your whole fridge is full. You stare at the one jar.{/reward}
old: My faith is mostly a list of things I cannot do.
new: Most of the garden is open. The limits are few and they protect me.
try: Write down five good things you are freely allowed to enjoy, and enjoy one of them today.

title: He sold the forbidden thing as an upgrade.
subtitle: The whisper that promises more
then: Shaytan wanted to strip them of {reward}the blessings and clothing they enjoyed{/reward}. So he whispered a lie: {trap}your Lord only forbade it to stop you becoming angels or living forever{/trap}. The forbidden thing was dressed up as the key to more.
now: The ad that says you deserve it. The voice that says one look will not hurt, and that the rule only exists because someone wants you to miss out. {trap}Same pitch, new packaging.{/trap}
old: Maybe the rule is there to keep me from something great.
new: The whisper always sells the forbidden thing as the thing I am missing.
try: When something tempts you today, ask who is selling it to you and what they want.

title: He swore by Allah he only wanted to help.
subtitle: Deception dressed as sincere advice

row.title: he swore, so it is true
an oath can be a trap

then: He swore by Allah that he was a sincere advisor. Qatada said he claimed: {trap}I was created before you and know more, so follow me{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}a believer can sometimes fall victim to deceit{/idea}.
now: The "trust me, I have been doing this for years" message about a quick money scheme. The friend who swears they only want what is best for you, while pushing you somewhere wrong. {idea}Strong promises are not proof.{/idea}
old: If someone swears they mean well, I should believe them.
new: Sincere words can wrap bad advice, so I check the advice itself.
try: Before acting on one piece of advice today, ask: does this lead toward Allah or away?

title: One taste, and what was covered was exposed.
subtitle: The fall, and the call that followed
then: Once they tasted the tree, {trap}their covering was gone{/trap}. They began to cover themselves with leaves; Ibn Abbas said fig leaves. {idea}Then their Lord called to them{/idea}, reminding them He had warned them that Shaytan was a clear enemy.
now: Right after the mistake, you feel exposed. You want to hide, to cover it up with whatever is near. {idea}Notice that the next thing in the story is not silence. It is a call.{/idea}
old: After I mess up, Allah does not want to hear from me.
new: Even right after the fall, my Lord still calls me back.
try: After your next slip, do not hide from prayer. Pray the very next one on time.

title: We wronged ourselves. Forgive us, or we are lost.
subtitle: The first repentance, and its words
then: Qatada said that Adam asked what would happen if he repented. {reward}Allah said He would admit him into Paradise.{/reward} Shaytan asked only for time, and {idea}each was given what he asked for{/idea}. Ad-Dahhak said these are the words Adam received from his Lord.
now: You said the harsh thing to your mother. You can explain why she pushed you to it. Or you can say: {reward}I was wrong, please forgive me.{/reward} {idea}Same moment, two very different requests.{/idea}
old: If I admit fault, I am giving up my side.
new: Owning my wrong and asking mercy is the way back, not a defeat.
try: Memorize this dua today: Rabbana zalamna anfusana, and say it once tonight.

title: Down to earth: a home and enjoyment, for a while.
subtitle: Earth as a stay with an end date
then: They were sent down to earth, with enmity now between people and Shaytan. The tafsir says {idea}each has a set term, written already{/idea}. It notes that the exact place of landing comes from Israelite tales, and {trap}if it mattered, Allah would have told us{/trap}.
now: The new flat, the new car, the new phone. Real enjoyment, and you are allowed it. {idea}But each one came with an end date you cannot see on the receipt.{/idea}
old: Life here is where I really live, and it will just go on.
new: Earth is a real home with real joy, but only for a set time.
try: Enjoy one good thing today on purpose, and thank Allah for it while it lasts.

title: Live here, die here, rise from here.
subtitle: The whole story of the ground beneath you
then: The tafsir connects this to another verse: {idea}from it We created you, into it We return you, from it We bring you out again{/idea}. On that Day, Allah gathers the first and the last and {reward}rewards each by their deeds{/reward}.
now: You walk past the cemetery on the way to work every morning and never look. {idea}The same ground under your shoes is where you will rest and where you will rise.{/idea}
old: The ground is just where I walk.
new: This same earth holds my life, my grave and my rising.
try: Next time you put your forehead on the ground in sujud, remember where you came from.

title: Clothes cover you. Taqwa covers you better.
subtitle: Two kinds of clothing, one is best
then: Right after the story of being exposed, Allah speaks to all of Adam's children. The tafsir says {reward}clothing to cover is essential, adornment is extra{/reward}. Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd said: {idea}when one fears Allah, Allah covers his errors{/idea}.
now: Twenty minutes choosing an outfit for the wedding, checking the mirror from every angle. {idea}There is another covering nobody sees in the mirror, and it hides more than any outfit can.{/idea}
old: Looking good is how I protect myself from people's eyes.
new: Clothes cover my body. Taqwa covers my faults.
try: While getting dressed tomorrow, ask Allah to clothe you in taqwa too.

title: He did it to your parents. He sees you now.
subtitle: An old enemy you cannot see

key.label: Who to take as an ally

then: The tafsir says this shows {trap}Shaytan's deep hatred{/trap} for Adam and his children. He moved Adam from the home of comfort to the home of hardship. It links the verse to one asking: {idea}will you take him as an ally instead of Me, when he is your enemy?{/idea}
now: You would never trust a stranger who had already robbed your family. Yet the same voice that tricked Adam still whispers to you at midnight. {trap}You cannot see him, but he sees you.{/trap}
old: What I cannot see cannot really affect me.
new: My oldest enemy is invisible and has a history with my family.
try: Say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim before opening your phone tonight.

title: Our fathers did it, so Allah must want it.
subtitle: Tradition used as a stamp of approval
then: Many Arabs went around the Ka'bah naked, saying they would not do tawaf in clothes they had sinned in. {trap}They claimed their fathers' habit was Allah's command.{/trap} The reply: {idea}Allah does not order indecency. Do you say about Him what you do not know?{/idea}
now: "This is just how our family does it." The way relatives treat daughters-in-law, the way money is handled at funerals. {trap}Then someone adds that it is religion.{/trap} {idea}A habit does not become Allah's word because it is old.{/idea}
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: Old habits need real proof before I say Allah wants them.
try: Pick one family custom you follow and ask honestly where it actually comes from.

title: What He does command: justice and sincere worship.
subtitle: The real orders, and the return

row.title: correct and sincere
sub: by His law, free of shirk

then: After rejecting their false claim, the verse says what Allah actually commands: {idea}justice, and worship made sincere to Him{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says a deed is accepted when it is {reward}correct by His law and free of shirk{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ said people will be gathered to Allah barefoot, as they were first created.
now: Your prayer is on time, but your mind is on who is watching. Or your heart is in it, but you made up your own way. {reward}The verse asks for both: done right, and done for Him.{/reward}
old: As long as my heart is in the right place, the method does not matter.
new: Allah wants worship done the right way and done only for Him.
try: In one prayer today, whisper before you start: this is only for You.

title: They followed devils and were sure they were guided.
subtitle: The danger of feeling certain
then: The verse ends the reply to those who made up their own worship. Ibn Abbas said Allah {idea}began people as believers and disbelievers, and returns them that way{/idea}. The worst part is the last line: {trap}they took devils as allies and thought they were guided{/trap}.
now: You are completely sure in the argument with your brother, so sure that you never stop to check. {trap}Certainty felt like proof.{/trap} {idea}Being sure and being guided are not the same thing.{/idea}
old: If I feel confident I am right, I do not need to check.
new: Feeling guided is not proof. I keep checking who I am following.
try: Ask Allah tonight, in your own words, to show you if you are wrong about something.

title: Dress well for prayer. Eat and drink, without excess.
subtitle: Beauty at the masjid, balance at the table
then: This answered the practice of going around the Ka'bah naked. Allah told people to {idea}take their adornment to every masjid{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said: {reward}eat and wear what you wish{/reward}, as long as you avoid two things, {trap}extravagance and arrogance{/trap}.
now: You throw on the gym hoodie for prayer, but you dress up for a dinner with friends. At that dinner you order three dishes and take half home to forget in the fridge. {idea}The verse flips both habits.{/idea}
old: Prayer clothes do not matter, and food is mine to waste.
new: I bring my best to Allah and stop at enough at the table.
try: Wear something clean and nice for your next prayer, and stop one meal before you are full.

title: Who forbade the good things Allah made for you?
subtitle: Beauty and good food are His gifts
then: The idolaters had banned certain foods and clothes {trap}from their own opinions, with no basis from Allah{/trap}. The verse asks who gave them that right. The tafsir says these gifts are {reward}for believers in this life, and only theirs in the next{/reward}.
now: Someone in your circle says wearing nice things or enjoying a good meal is not for real believers. You start feeling guilty over a new coat. {idea}Allah made beautiful things for His servants. Guilt was not part of the gift.{/idea}
old: Enjoying nice things must make me less religious.
new: Good things are Allah's gifts to His servants, meant to be enjoyed with thanks.
try: Enjoy one good thing today fully, and say alhamdulillah out loud for it.

title: What He really forbade is a short, serious list.
subtitle: Five things my Lord prohibited
then: After asking who forbade good things, the verse says what Allah did forbid. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}none is more protective than Allah{/idea}, which is why He forbade indecency, open or secret. Mujahid and others explained that {trap}sin harms yourself, oppression harms others{/trap}, and both are forbidden.
now: You argue online for an hour about which clothes are allowed. The same evening you snap at your sibling and forward a rumor about a coworker. {idea}The serious list was about the second part of your day.{/idea}
old: Religion is mostly about the small details of dress and food.
new: Allah's real lines are around harm, injustice, shirk and lies about Him.
try: Check today for one of these five in your own day: hidden sin, unfairness, or speaking about Allah without knowing.

title: Every people has a deadline. Not one hour early or late.
subtitle: A set term no one can move
then: The tafsir says every {idea}generation and nation has its appointed term{/idea}, which it was destined for. When it comes, {trap}they cannot delay it or bring it forward{/trap}, not even by an hour.
now: The calendar on your phone is full of plans for next year. None of them knows your real deadline. {idea}Neither does any doctor in any hospital corridor.{/idea} {trap}It will not move for unfinished business.{/trap}
old: I can always put off the important things for a while.
new: My term is fixed, so what I mean to do for Allah should not wait.
try: Do the one thing you would regret leaving undone, or start it, today.

title: Messengers came. Fear Allah, fix things, and fear nothing.
subtitle: No fear and no grief for the careful

row.title: taqwa and reform
sub: leave the bad, do the good

then: Right after the deadline, Allah reminds the children of Adam that He sent messengers with good news and warning. The tafsir explains taqwa and reform as {idea}leaving what is forbidden and doing what He asks{/idea}. For them: {reward}no fear and no grief{/reward}.
now: You lie awake doing the math on the mortgage, your kid's grades, your health check. {reward}The verse offers a quieter way to sleep{/reward}: be careful with Allah, and fix what is in your hands.
old: I will feel safe once everything in life is under control.
new: Real safety comes from taqwa and fixing what I can.
try: Fix one thing you have let slide, a debt, an apology, a prayer, today.

title: Denying the signs out of pride has a lasting cost.
subtitle: The other side of the same choice
then: Next to the promise of the last verse comes its opposite. The tafsir says {trap}their hearts denied the signs, and they were too arrogant to follow them{/trap}. The two paths are set side by side so the listener can choose.
now: Sometimes it is not that you do not know. You know prayer is due; you know the lie was wrong. {trap}What stops you is that changing feels like losing.{/trap} {idea}Notice that pride, and the door is still open.{/idea}
old: I would follow if the truth were only clearer.
new: Often the truth is clear and pride is what holds me back.
try: Do one good thing today that your pride has been resisting.

title: At death they ask: where are your helpers now?
subtitle: Every false support disappears at the end
then: Those who lie about Allah still get {reward}their share of provision and life{/reward}, the tafsir says, until death comes. Then the angels ask where the others they invoked have gone. They answer: {trap}they have vanished and deserted us{/trap}, and confess against themselves.
now: The boss you flatter, the connections, the savings, the lucky ritual you do before exams. {trap}All of it leaves the room at the end.{/trap} {idea}Ask now what you would answer if asked where they are.{/idea}
old: The people and things I rely on will carry me through.
new: Only Allah remains when every other support leaves.
try: Name one thing you lean on more than Allah, and give it back to its proper size today.

title: The followers blame their leaders. Each gets double.
subtitle: Blame does not lighten anyone's load
then: Each group that enters curses the one before it. The followers ask that their leaders get double, because {trap}these misled us{/trap}. The answer is that {idea}each one has double{/idea}, recompensed by their own deeds. The tafsir links it to verses where leaders and followers disown each other.
now: "Everyone in the office was doing it." "My friends pushed me." {trap}The blame feels like a shield.{/trap} {idea}The verse says it lightens no one: the one who led and the one who followed both carry their part.{/idea}
old: If someone else led me into it, it is mostly their fault.
new: Blaming the one who led me does not remove my own share.
try: Take ownership out loud of one thing you have been blaming on someone else.

title: You were no better than us, the leaders reply.
subtitle: No one is spared by pointing fingers
then: The leaders answer the followers' complaint. As-Suddi explained it as {trap}you were led astray as we were led astray{/trap}. Then comes the line: {idea}taste it for what you used to earn{/idea}.
now: The group chat that mocked someone. You did not start it; you only added the laughing emoji. {idea}Following is still a choice you made with your own thumb.{/idea}
old: Going along with the crowd makes me less responsible.
new: Following someone into wrong is still my own choice and my own earning.
try: The next time a group goes somewhere wrong today, stay quiet or walk away instead of joining.

title: A camel through a needle's eye. That closed a door.
subtitle: When pride shuts the gates of heaven

row.title: gates of heaven
sub: deeds and duas do not rise

then: Ibn Abbas and others said the gates not opening means {trap}their good deeds and duas will not rise{/trap}. Others said it refers to their souls; Ibn Jurayj combined both. The image of a camel through a needle's eye shows {idea}how impossible it is while the pride remains{/idea}.
now: You make dua, but never let go of the thing you know is wrong and refuse to admit. {idea}The verse is not about strangers. It asks whether your own pride is blocking your own door.{/idea}
old: My duas go up no matter how I treat Allah's signs.
new: Pride toward the truth can block the very door my duas go through.
try: Before your next dua, admit to Allah one thing you have been too proud to admit.

title: A bed beneath and coverings above, of fire.
subtitle: The recompense of the wrongdoers
then: Al-Qurazi explained the words as {trap}beds below and coverings over them{/trap}, from the Fire. The verse closes with {idea}thus do We recompense the wrongdoers{/idea}, after describing those who denied the signs with pride.
now: Tonight you will pull the blanket up and scroll before sleep. {idea}A warm bed is a mercy you did not earn.{/idea} {reward}It is also a good place to think about how you want to rest later.{/reward}
old: Comfort now means I am fine.
new: The rest I get later depends on what I do with my days now.
try: Before sleeping tonight, think over your day for one minute and seek forgiveness for one thing.

title: Believe, do good, and you are never asked too much.
subtitle: Paradise, within your capacity
then: After the warnings, the surah turns to the happy ones. The tafsir notes that in the middle of this promise Allah says {reward}He burdens no soul beyond its scope{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this shows {idea}that faith and acting on it are made easy{/idea}.
now: You look at people who pray the night and fast every Monday, and you think there is no point in starting. {reward}Allah never asked for their capacity. He asked for yours.{/reward}
old: If I cannot do it all, I should not bother trying.
new: Allah asks only what I can carry, and that is enough to start.
try: Pick one good deed small enough that you can do it daily this week, and do it today.

title: Every grudge removed, and they praise the One who guided.
subtitle: Paradise begins with clean hearts
then: The Prophet ﷺ said believers will be held at a bridge until {trap}wrongs between them are settled{/trap}, then enter Paradise. They praise Allah for guiding them. He ﷺ also said {reward}no one's deeds alone admit him, not even his own, unless Allah covers him with mercy{/reward}.
now: The cousin you have not spoken to since the inheritance fight. The friend who never paid you back. {idea}In Paradise, that weight is lifted off the chest.{/idea} You could start putting it down now.
old: Some grudges I will carry forever.
new: Paradise has no room for resentment, so letting go starts here.
try: Pray for one person you hold a grudge against, by name, today.

title: We found His promise true. Did you find yours?
subtitle: One question across the divide
then: The people of Paradise call across: {reward}we found our Lord's promise true{/reward}. Have you? They answer {trap}yes{/trap}. The tafsir recalls that after Badr, the Prophet ﷺ called the fallen leaders of Quraysh by name with the same question.
now: You hear about the Day and file it under "probably." You make plans for the weekend with far more certainty. {idea}One day everyone will say yes to this question. The difference is only when.{/idea}
old: The promises about the Hereafter are probably true, someday.
new: Every promise and warning from Allah will be found exactly true.
try: Read one verse about Paradise today and let yourself believe it fully for a minute.

title: They blocked the path and made it look crooked.
subtitle: Turning others away from Allah's way
then: The tafsir says they {trap}hindered people from Allah's path and made it appear crooked and winding{/trap}, so no one would follow. They denied the meeting with Allah, so {idea}they took evil words and deeds lightly{/idea}.
now: Your friend tries to start praying, and you joke that it will not last. Your sister wears hijab for the first time, and you roll your eyes. {idea}Small comments can make the straight path look crooked to someone.{/idea}
old: My little jokes about someone's faith are harmless.
new: My words can make Allah's path look easier or harder for others.
try: Encourage one person today who is trying to come closer to Allah.

title: On the heights between, people wait and hope.
subtitle: The people of Al-A'raf, after whom the surah is named

row.title: hoping
sub: a hope Allah placed in them

then: Between Paradise and the Fire is a wall with high places, Al-A'raf. Hudhayfah, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and others said those on it are {idea}people whose good and bad deeds are equal{/idea}. They greet the people of Paradise with peace. Al-Hasan said {reward}Allah only put this hope in their hearts because He means to honor them{/reward}.
now: You feel stuck in the middle: not bad enough to give up, not good enough to feel sure. A few prayers missed, a few kept. {reward}The verse gives the people in between hope, not shame.{/reward}
old: If I am only halfway good, I have no reason to hope.
new: Even those in between are given hope, and one more good deed tips the scale.
try: Add one good deed today that you would not normally do, for the scale.

title: They look toward the Fire and pray: not with them.
subtitle: A dua made while seeing the danger

row.title: turn to Allah
sub: ask Him to keep you apart

then: Ibn Abbas said that when they look at the people of the Fire and {trap}recognize them{/trap}, they make dua: {idea}O Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people{/idea}. Seeing the danger turns them straight to their Lord.
now: You see a friend's life fall apart from a habit you also have, maybe a gambling app or a temper. {idea}Seeing it is a warning, and the right response is a dua.{/idea}
old: Seeing others fall makes me feel either superior or hopeless.
new: When I see where a path leads, I ask Allah to keep me off it.
try: When you see someone's harmful habit today, quietly ask Allah to protect you from it too.

title: Your crowd and your pride, what did they get you?
subtitle: Numbers and status cannot save
then: The people on the heights call to chiefs of the idolaters they recognize. The tafsir says: {trap}your great numbers and wealth did not save you{/trap} from Allah's punishment. {idea}Their gathering and their pride had no value there.{/idea}
now: Followers, a big family name, a WhatsApp group of three hundred people who always take your side. {trap}It feels like protection.{/trap} {idea}None of it stands next to you when you are asked about your own life.{/idea}
old: With enough people behind me, I am safe.
new: Crowds and status buy nothing before Allah.
try: Do one thing today for Allah only, that no crowd will see or praise.

title: The ones you said would never get mercy: enter Paradise.
subtitle: Who receives mercy is not ours to swear

row.title: I can tell who is lost

then: The arrogant had sworn that {trap}Allah would never show these people mercy{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said this refers to the people of Al-A'raf. Then Allah decrees for them: {reward}enter Paradise, no fear on you, nor will you grieve{/reward}.
now: You have written someone off: the cousin who left the deen, the coworker with the past. You are sure how their story ends. {idea}The verse is a warning about that certainty.{/idea}
old: Some people are obviously beyond Allah's mercy.
new: I do not get to swear who Allah will have mercy on.
try: Think of one person you have written off and make a sincere dua for them.

title: Pour us some water. But that door is shut.
subtitle: A request that comes too late

row.title: I can ask for help later
now
sub: this life is when to earn it

then: Sa'id bin Jubayr said a man will call to {trap}his own father or brother, I am burning, pour water on me{/trap}. The reply is that Allah has forbidden both water and food of Paradise to the disbelievers. {idea}Family ties do not carry it across.{/idea}
now: You think your mother's prayers will cover you, or your pious brother. You will lean on them later. {idea}Their good is theirs. Yours you earn now, while water still flows for everyone.{/idea}
old: My pious relatives will be able to help me out on the Day.
new: What I need on the Day, I prepare now with my own deeds.
try: Give someone a glass of water or a drink today, and intend it for your own Day.

title: They forgot this Day, so today they are forgotten.
subtitle: Treating religion as play
then: They took their religion as amusement and play, {trap}deceived by this life{/trap}. The tafsir is clear that {idea}Allah never forgets anything{/idea}; it means they are left as they left Him. A hadith tells of a man reminded of his marriage and honor, who never thought he would meet Allah.
now: Prayer squeezed between episodes. Ramadan as a food season. {trap}Faith as one more app on the phone.{/trap} {idea}The Day you keep forgetting is the Day you will need to be remembered.{/idea}
old: Religion can be a light hobby while life is the real thing.
new: If I forget the meeting with Allah, I am forgetting the most serious thing.
try: Count three blessings you have, and say each one to Allah like the man in the hadith was reminded of his.

title: They were given a Book explained in detail.
subtitle: Guidance arrived, so there is no excuse
then: The tafsir says Allah {idea}left no excuse{/idea} for the idolaters: He sent them a Book explained in detail. He also says He does not punish until a messenger has come. {reward}The Book is guidance and mercy{/reward} for anyone who believes.
now: The Quran app is on your phone between the food delivery and the bank. Translation, tafsir, audio, all one tap away. {idea}The excuse of not knowing gets thinner every day.{/idea}
old: I would follow it better if I only understood it.
new: The Book is already explained in detail. I only need to open it.
try: Read the translation of one page of Quran today, slowly.

title: On the Day it comes true, they ask to go back.
subtitle: Wishing for one more chance
then: When the promised outcome arrives, those who ignored it admit {idea}the messengers came with the truth{/idea}. They ask for intercessors, or to be sent back to do differently. {trap}What they worshipped instead of Allah has left them.{/trap}
now: Today is the "send us back" they will wish for. You are already in it. {reward}Every morning you wake up is the second chance someone else is begging for.{/reward}
old: I will change once I am really sure.
new: Today is the chance to do differently that others will wish they had.
try: Do one thing today you would want to have done if you could come back.

title: Creation and command are His. Night chases day.
subtitle: Your Lord, the Lord of the worlds
then: After warnings about the Day, the surah turns to who your Lord is. Ibn Kathir follows the early scholars on rising over the Throne: {idea}accept it as stated, without likening Him to creation or denying it{/idea}. Night and day {reward}follow each other, never late{/reward}, all under His command.
now: You watch the sunset from the bus window, and sunrise from your alarm. {idea}Not once has the night forgotten to come.{/idea} The same Lord who runs that runs your Monday.
old: The universe is just running on its own.
new: Every sunrise and sunset is His command, and so is my life.
try: Watch one sunset or sunrise this week and say tabarakallah, rabbul alamin.

title: Call on Him humbly and quietly. He is near.
subtitle: How to make dua
then: Right after showing His power, Allah tells His servants to call on Him. When people raised their voices in dua, the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}you are not calling one who is deaf or absent; He is All-Hearing, Near{/reward}. Scholars said transgressing in dua includes {trap}asking for the rank of the Prophets{/trap}.
now: Lying in bed after a long shift, too tired for a long prayer, you think it does not count. {reward}A whispered sentence into the pillow reaches Him.{/reward}
old: Dua only counts if it is loud, long and formal.
new: A humble, quiet dua reaches the One who is near.
try: Tonight, whisper one honest dua before you sleep.

title: Do not spoil what was set right. Pray in fear and hope.
subtitle: His mercy is near the doers of good

row.title: both together
sub: fear His punishment, hope His reward

then: The tafsir says mischief after things are set in order {trap}causes the most harm to people{/trap}. Call on Him {idea}fearing His punishment and hoping for His reward{/idea}. Matar Al-Warraq said: earn His promise by obeying Him, for {reward}His mercy is near the good-doers{/reward}.
now: The family finally made peace after years. Then one sarcastic comment at the dinner table. {trap}It took a minute to undo a year.{/trap} {reward}Doing good keeps you close to His mercy.{/reward}
old: One small comment cannot ruin things that are already fixed.
new: What has been set right deserves protecting, and good keeps mercy near.
try: Protect one relationship that is in a good place today with a kind word.

title: Rain on dead land: that is how the dead will rise.
subtitle: A sign you can watch outside your window

row.title: resurrection
sub: so will We bring out the dead

then: After telling people to call on Him, Allah shows He is able. Winds go {reward}before His mercy, the rain{/reward}, driven to dry land with no plants. The tafsir says {idea}just as dead land is brought to life, He will raise the dead{/idea}, a comparison the Quran often makes.
now: The park was brown all summer. One week of rain and it is green again. {idea}You did not think of the grave. The verse wants you to.{/idea} {reward}And of the hope in it.{/reward}
old: Rain is just weather.
new: Every rain on dry ground is a picture of the Resurrection.
try: Next time it rains, stop and look at it for a minute and remember this verse.

title: Same rain, different soil. Good land grows easily.
subtitle: What kind of ground is your heart?
then: The good land grows quickly and well, and the bad land {trap}brings out little, with difficulty{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ compared his guidance to {idea}abundant rain on different kinds of ground{/idea}. Some soaked it up and grew, some held it for others, and {trap}some held nothing{/trap}.
now: Two people sit through the same Friday khutbah. One goes home and calls his mother. The other is checking scores before the sermon ends. {idea}Same rain. Different soil.{/idea}
old: If I just hear more reminders, I will change.
new: The question is not how much guidance falls on me, but whether my heart takes it in.
try: After the next reminder you hear, write down one thing to act on, and do it.

title: Nuh's first words: worship Allah, I fear for you.
subtitle: The first messenger after Adam
then: After Adam, the surah begins the stories of the prophets with Nuh, {idea}the first messenger sent to the people of the earth after Adam{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said idol worship began when people made images of righteous men to remember them, and {trap}over time they worshipped them{/trap}. Nuh's first words were about Allah, and then {reward}his fear for them{/reward}.
now: It starts small. Love for a righteous person. Then their picture is treated as lucky. Then one day someone asks them for help instead of Allah. {idea}Nuh's message begins where that drift begins.{/idea}
old: Respect for good people can never become a problem.
new: Even love for righteous people can drift into worship if no one watches.
try: Ask yourself if anything in your life gets a little of what belongs only to Allah.

title: The chiefs looked at him and saw clear error.
subtitle: When the right one is called lost
then: The leaders said he was in plain error {trap}because he called them away from idols their forefathers worshipped{/trap}. The tafsir says {idea}this is the way of evil people: they see the righteous as misguided{/idea}.
now: You stop going to the Friday night party. Friends say you have gone weird, too religious, lost. {idea}Being called lost by the crowd is an old story.{/idea}
old: If everyone says I am wrong, I probably am.
new: The people who call me lost may be looking from the wrong place.
try: Stay firm on one good choice today even if someone mocks it.

title: No error in me. I am sent by the Lord of all.
subtitle: A calm answer to an insult

row.title: I am a messenger
sub: from the Lord of the worlds

then: Nuh did not insult them back. He said {reward}O my people{/reward}, and that there was nothing wrong with him. {idea}He was a messenger from the Lord and King of all things.{/idea}
now: Someone in the comments calls you an extremist for a simple post about prayer. Your thumb is ready with a sharp reply. {reward}Nuh still said "my people."{/reward}
old: If someone insults me, I have the right to hit back.
new: I can answer an insult calmly, still calling them my people.
try: Answer the next rude comment you get with one calm, kind sentence, or not at all.

title: I deliver, I advise sincerely, I know what you do not.
subtitle: Three marks of a messenger

row.title: you will be asked about me

then: The tafsir says these are the qualities of a messenger: {idea}clear delivery, sincere advice, knowledge of Allah{/idea}. At Arafah the Prophet ﷺ asked the huge crowd what they would say about him. They said {reward}you conveyed and advised sincerely{/reward}, and he said, O Allah, bear witness.
now: Someone you love is heading somewhere bad. You can lecture, shame, or post about it. {reward}Or you can be what Nuh was: clear, sincere, and caring.{/reward}
old: Giving advice means proving that I am right.
new: Real advice is clear, sincere, and for the other person's good.
try: Give one sincere piece of advice today, privately and gently.

title: Are you surprised the reminder came through one of you?
subtitle: Mercy delivered by a familiar face

row.title: one of you
sub: a kindness, not a strange thing

then: The tafsir says it is not strange that Allah sends revelation {reward}to a man among you, as mercy, kindness and compassion{/reward}. He was sent so they would avoid punishment and receive mercy. They were surprised it came from someone so ordinary.
now: Your little brother reminds you it is time for Asr. Your coworker mentions charity. {trap}You roll your eyes: who are they to tell me?{/trap} {idea}A reminder from a familiar face is still from your Lord.{/idea}
old: I only take reminders from people more impressive than me.
new: A reminder can come from anyone, and it is still a mercy.
try: Thank the next person who reminds you of something good, even if they are younger than you.

title: The ship saved the few. The blind were drowned.
subtitle: Blindness to the truth, and its end
then: They kept rejecting him, and {trap}only a few believed{/trap}. Allah saved Nuh and those with him in the ship. The tafsir explains "blind" as {trap}blind to the truth, unable to find their way to it{/trap}. It calls this {reward}Allah's way: the good end is for those who fear Him{/reward}.
now: The doctor warns you about your blood pressure three times. You stop going to appointments. {trap}Blindness is not always in the eyes.{/trap} {reward}The ship is still there for whoever gets on.{/reward}
old: I can always see the truth when I need to.
new: Refusing to look can make me blind to what is plain.
try: Face one warning you have been avoiding, about health, money or faith, today.

title: To Aad, their brother Hud, with the same words.
subtitle: A new people, the same message
then: Aad were a mighty people who lived in sand hills in Yemen, in the area of Ahqaf. Allah sent them {reward}their brother Hud{/reward}, from their noblest families. The tafsir says {trap}they were strong in body, and hard in heart{/trap}.
now: Your sister is the one who tells you to fix your prayer. Not a famous preacher, just her, at the kitchen table. {reward}Allah often sends the message through a brother or a sister.{/reward}
old: Good advice from family is just nagging.
new: Allah often sends His message through someone close to me.
try: Listen fully, without interrupting, to the next reminder a family member gives you.

title: Foolish and a liar, said the proud chiefs.
subtitle: Labels used to dodge the message
then: The arrogant chiefs called Hud {trap}foolish, and a liar{/trap}, because he asked them to leave idols for Allah alone. The tafsir notes {idea}Quraysh later wondered the same thing{/idea}: has he made all the gods one God?
now: Someone makes a point you cannot answer, so you call them a fanatic and change the subject. {trap}A label is the fastest way to avoid a question.{/trap}
old: If I can call someone a name, I do not have to listen to them.
new: Calling a person foolish never answers what they said.
try: When you disagree with someone today, answer their point instead of labeling them.

title: No foolishness in me, only a message from your Lord.
subtitle: Hud answers without bitterness

row.title: a messenger
sub: from the Lord of the worlds

then: Like Nuh before him, Hud said {reward}O my people{/reward}, and simply denied the charge. The tafsir says: {idea}I brought you the truth from Allah, who created everything{/idea}. He defended the message, not his ego.
now: Your manager says your idea is stupid in front of everyone. You want to prove how smart you are. {idea}Hud's move was quieter: make it about the truth, not about you.{/idea}
old: When I am insulted, I need to defend my image.
new: I can let the insult pass and keep pointing to what is true.
try: Next time you are criticized, ask "is it true?" before "how dare they?"

title: I am an adviser you can trust.
subtitle: Sincere and honest, even when rejected
then: They had called him a liar. Hud answered that {reward}he was a trustworthy adviser{/reward}. The tafsir says {idea}conveying, sincerity and honesty{/idea} are the qualities of the prophets.
now: You are the friend people come to when they need honest advice. That trust took years and can be lost in one lie. {reward}Being trustworthy is part of carrying any truth.{/reward}
old: Honesty is nice, but results matter more.
new: Being trusted is part of the message, not separate from it.
try: Keep one small promise today exactly as you made it.

title: Remember who you replaced, and what you were given.
subtitle: Strength as a favor to remember
then: Hud told them: {idea}rather than wonder, thank Allah{/idea} for sending you a messenger. He reminded them they came after Nuh's people, who were destroyed, and {reward}were given great stature{/reward}. Remembering favors is the way to success.
now: You are healthy, young, earning well, living where the last tenant could not afford to stay. {trap}It is easy to feel it is all you.{/trap} {idea}Hud's advice: remember who gave it.{/idea}
old: My strength and position are just how I am.
new: My strength is a favor, and remembering it is how I stay on track.
try: List three strengths you have today and thank Allah for each one.

title: Leave what our fathers worshipped? Bring the punishment, then.
subtitle: Daring the warning instead of heeding it
then: They refused to leave their fathers' idols and {trap}dared Hud to bring the punishment{/trap}. The tafsir notes the disbelievers of Quraysh later said the same: {trap}if this is the truth, rain stones on us{/trap}.
now: "If smoking were so bad, my grandfather would not have lived to 90." "Show me the damage, then." {idea}A warning is a door to walk through, not a bluff to call.{/idea}
old: If the warning were real, I would have seen it happen already.
new: A warning is given so I never have to see it happen.
try: Take one warning you have been daring, and quietly act on it today.

title: You argue for names you made up. Then wait.
subtitle: Idols with no authority behind them

row.title: names
sub: given by you and your fathers

row.title: an old name
sub: we have always called it that

then: Ibn Ishaq said they worshipped idols with names like Suda' and Samud. Hud asked: {trap}do you argue with me over names you and your fathers made{/trap}, which neither harm nor benefit? {idea}Allah sent no authority for them.{/idea} Then he said: wait, and I will wait with you.
now: "Lucky" numbers, a charm on the rearview mirror, a horoscope in the morning feed. {trap}Names with nothing behind them.{/trap} {idea}Ask what authority makes them matter.{/idea}
old: If something has a name and a history, it must have power.
new: A name with no proof from Allah behind it has no real power.
try: Remove one small superstition from your routine today.

title: Hud saved by mercy. The deniers cut off at the root.
subtitle: How the strongest people ended
then: Ibn Ishaq said Aad spread across the land with their strength, and {trap}built high palaces with no real use{/trap}. Only a few followed Hud, {reward}hiding their faith{/reward}. Allah saved them by mercy and ended the deniers with a violent wind.
now: You look at the people with power and money and think they are untouchable. Or you feel that way yourself. {idea}The strongest people in the story asked who was stronger than them. They had their answer.{/idea}
old: Strength and money keep you safe.
new: Allah's mercy is what saves, not strength.
try: Use one kind of strength you have today, time, money or health, to help someone weaker.

title: The sign they asked for: a camel. Leave her be.
subtitle: Salih and the she-camel of Allah

key.label: What a sign asks of you

then: Thamud lived between the Hijaz and Sham, after Aad. They asked Salih for a camel to come out of a rock they chose, and {idea}promised to believe if it happened{/idea}. It did. When the Prophet ﷺ passed their ruins on the way to Tabuk, he told his Companions {trap}not to enter unless weeping{/trap}, fearing the same might befall them.
now: You prayed for the job and promised to be better if you got it. You got it. {idea}The sign arrived. The real test is what you do with it now.{/idea}
old: If Allah just showed me a sign, I would change.
new: When the sign comes, the test is whether I honor it.
try: Recall one dua Allah answered, and keep one promise you made when you asked.

title: Palaces on the plains, homes cut in mountains. Remember who gave.
subtitle: Skill and wealth as reasons to remember
then: Salih reminded them they came {reward}after Aad{/reward}, who had been destroyed. They were skilled builders who cut homes into mountains. He asked them to {idea}remember Allah's favors{/idea} and {trap}not spread corruption in the land{/trap}.
now: You renovated the kitchen, got the promotion, finally moved to the nice area. {idea}Every new skill and room is a favor with a question attached: what will you do with it?{/idea}
old: What I build with my own skill is my own achievement.
new: My skills and homes are favors to remember, not reasons to forget.
try: In the room you are proudest of at home, say alhamdulillah and use it to host someone.

title: The proud asked the weak: are you really sure?
subtitle: Mockery aimed at those who believed
then: The arrogant leaders turned to the ones they {trap}looked down on as weak{/trap}, the ones who believed. Do you really know Salih is sent from his Lord? {reward}They did not argue about Salih. They simply said: we believe in what he was sent with.{/reward}
now: A colleague smirks: "Do you seriously believe all that?" You feel small, the junior one, the only one fasting. {reward}You do not need a debate. A calm "yes, I do" is enough.{/reward}
old: If I cannot win the argument, I should keep quiet about my faith.
new: A simple, calm "I believe" is a complete answer.
try: If someone questions your faith today, answer with one calm sentence and leave it there.

title: Whatever you believe in, we reject.
subtitle: When pride decides before the facts

key.label: What their answer was based on

then: The arrogant did not answer the believers' point. They said {trap}we disbelieve in whatever you believe in{/trap}. The camel was right in front of them. {idea}Their pride had decided before the evidence could.{/idea}
now: Your younger cousin suggests a better way to do something at the family business. You reject it before he finishes, because he is the young one. {trap}Pride was answering, not you.{/trap}
old: I judge ideas fairly on their merits.
new: Pride can make me reject truth only because of who said it.
try: Seriously consider one idea today from someone you usually dismiss.

title: They killed the camel and dared Salih to act.
subtitle: A whole people agreed to one crime
then: The camel drank one day and left the well to them the next, and {reward}they drank her milk{/reward}. They wanted the water every day, so they plotted to kill her. Qatadah said the killer {trap}checked with everyone, even women and children, and all agreed{/trap}. So the verse says they killed her, all together.
now: One person in the office writes the unfair email about a colleague. Five others read it in the draft and say nothing. {trap}Agreement is a share of the deed.{/trap}
old: I did not do it, I only agreed.
new: Agreeing to a wrong makes me part of it.
try: Withdraw your agreement from one wrong thing you have quietly gone along with.

title: The earth shook, and their homes became their graves.
subtitle: The end of Thamud
then: They had dared Salih to bring the punishment. {trap}The earthquake seized them, and they lay fallen in their homes.{/trap} The same homes they had carved so skillfully from mountains. {idea}The ruins were still there when the Prophet ﷺ passed by.{/idea}
now: The house with the alarm system, the insurance, the backup savings. Good things, wise things. {idea}But safety was never in the walls.{/idea}
old: With the right walls and plans, I am safe.
new: No home is safe against Allah's command; my safety is with Him.
try: Say the dua for leaving home today, trusting your safety to Allah.

title: I advised you, but you do not like advisers.
subtitle: Salih's last words to his people
then: Salih turned away and spoke to them after they had perished. Ibn Kathir compares it to the Prophet ﷺ speaking to the fallen leaders at Badr. Salih said he had {reward}conveyed and advised{/reward}, but {trap}they did not like the truth or those who gave sincere advice{/trap}.
now: Your friend tells you gently that the way you speak to your kids is harsh. You go cold on her for a week. {trap}You did not dislike the advice. You disliked the adviser.{/trap}
old: People who correct me are just being negative.
new: Disliking advisers is a quiet way of shutting out the truth.
try: Thank the last person who corrected you, sincerely, today.

title: Lut asked: a shameful act no one did before you?
subtitle: A people who invented a new indecency
then: Lut was {idea}the nephew of Ibrahim{/idea}, who believed in him and migrated with him. He was sent to Sodom and the villages around it. The tafsir says they {trap}practiced an indecency no one before them had done{/trap}.
now: Some wrongs grow because someone starts them and others copy. {trap}The person who begins a bad habit in a family or office carries a heavy share.{/trap} {idea}Ask what you are starting that others might follow.{/idea}
old: Being the first to do something is always brave.
new: Starting a wrong that others follow is its own heavy burden.
try: Start one good habit at home or work today that others could copy.

title: Desire followed past every limit. A people who went too far.
subtitle: Putting things where they do not belong
then: Lut said they went to men with desire instead of women. The tafsir says this {trap}placed things in their improper places{/trap}. He reminded them of the women of the nation, {idea}lawful to marry{/idea}, and they refused. His last word on them: {trap}a people transgressing beyond bounds{/trap}.
now: Your own desires push too: the late-night scroll, the second look, the food you said you would not eat. {idea}The question the verse leaves you is whether desire is driving, or you are.{/idea}
old: If I want something strongly, that makes it right for me.
new: Desire is real, but Allah's limits decide where it goes.
try: Say no to one desire today that you know goes past a limit, and say why to yourself.

title: Throw them out. They want to stay pure.
subtitle: When purity becomes the accusation
then: They gave no argument. Their only answer was to {trap}drive Lut and the believers out{/trap}. Qatadah said: {reward}they shamed them with what is not a shame at all{/reward}. Their charge was that they wanted to stay pure.
now: You leave the room when the jokes turn filthy. Later you are the one being talked about: "Too good for us, is he?" {reward}Being mocked for staying clean is not a mark against you.{/reward}
old: If they mock me for something, it must be embarrassing.
new: Sometimes I am mocked for exactly the thing I should keep.
try: Keep one clean habit today even if it makes you the odd one out.

title: Saved with his family, except the wife who stayed behind.
subtitle: Being close to a prophet is not enough
then: Only Lut's household believed in him. The tafsir says {trap}his wife stayed on her people's religion and signaled to them who visited him{/trap}. So he was told to leave at night without her, and {trap}she remained with those destroyed{/trap}.
now: Your father is the imam, your aunt teaches Quran, your husband prays every night. {idea}None of that is your own deed.{/idea} {trap}You can live in a believing house and still stay behind.{/trap}
old: Being from a religious family keeps me safe.
new: Only my own faith and deeds save me, not who I live with.
try: Do one act of worship today that is entirely your own, not part of a family routine.

title: A rain came down on them. See how it ended.
subtitle: An end to look at and learn from
then: The tafsir explains the rain through another verse: {trap}stones of baked clay, one after another{/trap}. Then the verse says "see". It addresses the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}look at the end of those who dared to disobey Allah and reject His messengers{/idea}.
now: News of a disaster lights up your feed, and the comments rush to say who deserved it. {idea}The verse asks you to look, then look at yourself.{/idea}
old: Stories of punishment are about other people.
new: I look at how others ended to fix my own path.
try: After reading any story of a ruined people, name one change in yourself it points to.

title: Give full measure. Do not short people their due.
subtitle: Shu'ayb's call to honest dealing
then: Madyan was a tribe and a city on the route from Sham to the Hijaz. Their sin was {trap}cheating in buying and selling, giving less in weight and measure{/trap}. Shu'ayb joined belief in Allah with {idea}honest dealing{/idea}. He was called {reward}the speaker of the prophets{/reward} for his eloquence.
now: The invoice padded by an hour. The used car sold without mentioning the noise. The shift where you clocked in and scrolled. {trap}The scale is not only in the market.{/trap}
old: Small shortcuts in business are just how things work.
new: Giving people their full due is part of my faith in Allah.
try: Check one deal, bill or timesheet this week and make sure it is exactly fair.

title: Do not sit on every road to threaten people.
subtitle: Blocking others, and forgetting you were once few
then: As-Suddi said they were {trap}bandits, threatening people on the roads for their money{/trap}. Others said they threatened those coming to follow Shu'ayb. He reminded them: {reward}you were few and weak, and He made you many{/reward}.
now: You finally have some power: the team lead, the landlord, the older sibling. {trap}It is tempting to sit at the gate and make others pay to pass.{/trap} {reward}Remember when you were the new one.{/reward}
old: Now that I have the upper hand, I can set the terms.
new: My strength came from Allah's favor, so I do not block others with it.
try: Make one thing easier today for someone who depends on you.

title: Divided over me? Be patient until Allah judges.
subtitle: Leaving the verdict to the best of judges
then: Shu'ayb's people were split. He told them: {idea}be patient until Allah judges between us{/idea}. The tafsir says Allah {reward}gives the best end to those who fear and obey Him{/reward}.
now: The family is split over a decision you made for the sake of your faith. Every dinner is a debate. {idea}You do not have to win every round. Some verdicts belong to Allah.{/idea}
old: I have to settle every disagreement myself, now.
new: I can stand firm, be patient, and leave the verdict to Allah.
try: Drop one argument today that you keep trying to win, and leave it with Allah.

title: Leave town or come back to our ways.
subtitle: The chiefs' ultimatum to Shuayb
then: The arrogant chiefs of Shuayb's people threatened to expel him and those who believed with him, {trap}or force them back to the old religion.{/trap} The words were aimed at Shuayb but meant for his followers too. His calm reply: {idea}Even if we are unwilling?{/idea}
now: Your friends say you have changed since you started praying. Come out like before, or we stop inviting you. {trap}It is framed as a choice, but it is pressure.{/trap} {idea}You are allowed to say no kindly.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me pushes, I will have to give in eventually.
new: Pressure can move my body, but it cannot make my heart love what it left.
try: Think of one place you hide your faith to fit in. Show it a little, gently, once today.

title: Upon Allah we rely. Judge between us.
subtitle: Shuayb hands the outcome to Allah
then: Shuayb told them that returning would be {trap}inventing a lie against Allah{/trap} after He had saved them from it. He left every matter to Allah's will and knowledge. Then he turned to Allah: {reward}upon You we rely, judge between us and our people in truth.{/reward}
now: A relative spreads a twisted version of your family fight on the group chat. You draft a long reply at 1 a.m. {trap}You want to win it tonight.{/trap} {reward}You could also put the phone down and ask the Best of Judges.{/reward}
old: If I do not defend myself loudly, the truth will lose.
new: I can stay firm, say what is true, and leave the verdict with Allah.
try: Before replying to one argument today, make a short dua and wait an hour.

title: Follow him and you will lose, they warned.
subtitle: The chiefs' fear campaign
then: Ibn Kathir says this shows the depth of defiance in their hearts. The chiefs vowed to the people that {trap}following Shuayb would make them losers.{/trap} Allah answered that claim with what came next, and {idea}the verses that follow turn the word losers back on those who said it.{/idea}
now: Someone at work tells you that being honest in sales will cost you your bonus. Everyone cuts corners, they say. {trap}You will lose if you do not.{/trap} {idea}Ask who really ends up losing.{/idea}
old: Doing right will make me fall behind.
new: The ones who warn me about losing are not the ones who decide who loses.
try: Do one honest thing today that might cost you a little. Notice how it feels after.

title: The town they guarded became their grave.
subtitle: The end that answered their threat
then: They threatened to drive Shuayb and the believers out of the town. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}the earthquake shook them as punishment for that threat.{/trap} Other surahs mention a cry and a dark cloud on the same day. {idea}The ones who wanted to expel others were the ones removed.{/idea}
now: You feel secure in your house, your job, your health. It is easy to look down on someone with less. {trap}Security can make you hard.{/trap} {idea}What you stand on is held up by Allah, not by you.{/idea}
old: My home and position are solid. They are mine.
new: Everything I stand on is lent, and can change in a single night.
try: Thank Allah out loud tonight for the roof over you, by name.

title: As if they had never lived there at all.
subtitle: The word losers returned to its owners
then: The chiefs had wanted to expel Shuayb from the land. After the punishment, {trap}it was as though they had never lived in it.{/trap} Ibn Kathir notes Allah refuted their earlier claim directly: {idea}those who denied Shuayb, they were the losers.{/idea}
now: Walk past a shop that was the busiest on your street ten years ago. Now it is a phone repair stall and nobody remembers the name. {trap}Status fades fast.{/trap} {idea}What you did with it is what stays.{/idea}
old: The people with power now will always be there.
new: Power that denies the truth leaves no trace worth keeping.
try: Think of something you are building. Ask if it will matter when your name is forgotten.

title: I told you, I advised you. I did my part.
subtitle: Shuayb turns away after the end
then: After the destruction, Shuayb turned away from his people. He told them {idea}I conveyed my Lord's messages and gave you good advice.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: I delivered what I was sent with, {trap}so I will not grieve, since you rejected it.{/trap}
now: You warned your younger brother about the friends he was keeping. You said it kindly, more than once. He did not listen. {trap}You keep blaming yourself.{/trap} {idea}You did your part. The rest was his.{/idea}
old: If they did not change, I must have failed.
new: My job is to advise sincerely. Their response is not my burden to carry.
try: Think of one person you keep trying to fix. Make dua for them, then let go a little.

title: Hardship came so they might turn back.
subtitle: The purpose behind difficulty
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the nations who denied their Prophets were struck with {trap}sickness, poverty and humiliation{/trap}, so they might supplicate and humble themselves. The hardship was a door. {idea}It was meant to bring them to Allah.{/idea}
now: The rent is late. Your knee will not heal. The job offer fell through. {trap}You scroll to forget.{/trap} {idea}What if this week is asking you to raise your hands, not numb yourself?{/idea}
old: Hard times are just something to get through.
new: Hard times can be an invitation to come back to Allah humbly.
try: Take the hardest thing in your life right now and ask Allah about it, plainly, in your own words.

title: Good times and bad, they called it a cycle.
subtitle: Failing both tests
then: After hardship, Allah gave them health and plenty until they grew in number and wealth. They said {trap}our fathers also had hard and easy times{/trap}, as if it were only a cycle. Ibn Kathir quotes the hadith that the believer's affair is all good: {idea}patient in harm, thankful in ease.{/idea}
now: Last year you were broke. This year you got the promotion. You tell yourself the economy turned. {trap}No lesson either time.{/trap} {idea}Both seasons were questions. Patience then, gratitude now.{/idea}
old: Life just goes up and down. That is how it works.
new: Every season, hard or easy, is a test with a right answer.
try: Name one good thing in your life right now and thank Allah for it specifically.

title: Faith and taqwa open the sky and earth.
subtitle: What could have been for those towns

row.title: blessings
sub: rain from sky, growth from earth

then: Ibn Kathir notes how little faith the towns had, except the people of Yunus. Had they believed and kept taqwa, {reward}Allah would have opened blessings from the sky and the earth{/reward}, meaning rain and crops. {trap}But they denied, and were taken for what they earned.{/trap}
now: You work overtime, chase side hustles, refresh your bank app. There is never quite enough. {trap}You keep pushing harder.{/trap} {reward}Barakah is not only about more hours. It comes from how you live before Allah.{/reward}
old: More work is the only way to get more.
new: Faith and mindfulness of Allah are part of how blessing reaches me.
try: Give a small amount in charity today and pray on time once, with your provision in mind.

title: What if it came while you slept?
subtitle: The false safety of the night
then: Allah asks the people of the towns a sharp question: {trap}did they feel secure that His punishment would not come at night while they slept?{/trap} Ibn Kathir describes it as a warning against defying His orders. {idea}The question is meant to wake the heart.{/idea}
now: You plug in your phone and pull up the blanket. The apology you owe, the prayer you skipped, the debt you have not returned. {trap}Tomorrow, you think.{/trap} {idea}Sleep is the one thing you do every night without knowing you will wake.{/idea}
old: I will sort my life out later. There is time.
new: No night is guaranteed, so I settle what matters before I sleep.
try: Before bed tonight, fix one small thing you have been putting off. Then sleep easy.

title: Or in broad daylight, while busy playing?
subtitle: The false safety of a busy day
then: After the night, the day. Did they feel secure that it would not come {trap}in the forenoon while they were at play{/trap}? Ibn Kathir explains: while busy in their affairs and unaware. {idea}Night or day, asleep or busy, no hour is outside Allah's reach.{/idea}
now: Mid-morning. Meetings, messages, the school run, a game on your break. {trap}Allah does not cross your mind until evening.{/trap} {idea}The busiest hour is exactly when remembering Him counts.{/idea}
old: When I am busy, faith can wait until I am free.
new: Busy hours are not safe hours. I can remember Allah inside them.
try: Set one reminder for the middle of your busiest hour tomorrow: say a quiet dhikr when it rings.

title: Only losers feel safe from Allah's plan.
subtitle: Healthy fear versus careless comfort
then: The third question: did they feel secure from Allah's plan? {trap}None feel secure from it except the losers.{/trap} Ibn Kathir quotes Al-Hasan Al-Basri: {idea}the believer worships while still feeling fear and concern, while the wicked sins and feels safe.{/idea}
now: You notice you have stopped feeling bad about the small lies at work. They have become normal. {trap}That comfort is the warning sign.{/trap} {idea}A little concern in your chest is a sign your heart is still alive.{/idea}
old: If I feel no guilt, I must be fine.
new: Feeling too safe while doing wrong is the real danger.
try: Name one habit you no longer feel uneasy about. Ask whether you should.

title: You live where others fell. Does that not guide you?
subtitle: Inheriting the land and the lesson
then: Ibn Jarir explained: those who settled the land after earlier nations were destroyed then followed the same ways. Did it not become clear to them that {trap}Allah could punish them too for their sins?{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to verses about walking in the dwellings of those before. {idea}The past is a guide, if the heart can still hear.{/idea}
now: You take over your late uncle's business. You saw how his temper drove people away. {trap}Within a year you are shouting at staff the same way.{/trap} {idea}You inherited the shop. You can choose not to inherit the mistake.{/idea}
old: What happened to people before me has nothing to do with me.
new: I walk where others walked, and their story is a warning I can hear.
try: Name one mistake you saw in someone before you. Do the opposite once today.

title: Rejecting it the first time makes the next harder.
subtitle: Why clear proofs did not change them
then: After the stories of Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shuayb, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}these are the towns whose news We relate to you.{/idea} Their Messengers came with clear proofs. Ibn Kathir explains, citing Ibn Atiyyah, that {trap}they would not believe later because they denied the truth when it first came{/trap}, even though they recognized it.
now: Your friend points out, gently, that you talk over people. You brush it off. Next time it is easier to brush off. {trap}Each no makes the next no automatic.{/trap} {idea}The first time you hear the truth is the easiest time to accept it.{/idea}
old: I can always accept it later, when I am ready.
new: Every time I push the truth away, my heart gets a little harder to open.
try: Think of one piece of honest feedback you dismissed. Reconsider it today.

title: Most of them forgot the first promise.
subtitle: The covenant written into every person
then: Allah found most of those nations not true to their covenant. Ibn Kathir explains it as {idea}the fitrah, the pledge taken from them that Allah alone is their Lord.{/idea} He quotes the hadith that every child is born on the fitrah. {trap}They threw that covenant behind their backs{/trap} with no proof.
now: Watch a small child stare at the night sky and ask who made the stars. Then watch the world teach them to stop asking. {trap}The question gets buried under noise.{/trap} {idea}It is still in you.{/idea}
old: Faith is something I have to build from nothing.
