new: Faith is a promise already inside me that I can return to.
try: Spend two quiet minutes outside tonight looking up. Let the old question come back.

title: They knew the signs were true and still refused.
subtitle: Musa sent to Firaun and his chiefs
then: After Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shuayb, Allah sent Musa with clear signs to Firaun, the ruler of Egypt, and his chiefs. {trap}They rejected them out of injustice and stubbornness.{/trap} Ibn Kathir cites another verse: they denied the signs though they were convinced of them inside. {idea}See how the corrupters ended.{/idea}
now: You know your partner is right about the money. You can see it in the numbers. {trap}But admitting it feels like losing.{/trap} {idea}Pride can make you argue against what you already know.{/idea}
old: I would accept the truth if it were clear enough.
new: Sometimes the truth is clear, and only my pride stands in the way.
try: Admit you were wrong about one small thing today, out loud, to the person concerned.

title: A Messenger from the Lord of all the worlds.
subtitle: Musa introduces himself to Firaun
then: Ibn Kathir describes a debate between Musa and Firaun before his people. Musa opened plainly: {idea}I am a Messenger from the Lord of all that exists{/idea}, meaning the One who sent me is Creator, Lord and King of all things. {trap}He said it to a man who claimed lordship himself.{/trap}
now: You walk into your manager's office to raise something unfair. Your hands are shaking. {trap}The person behind the desk feels like everything.{/trap} {idea}Remember who is above every desk.{/idea}
old: The most powerful person in the room decides my fate.
new: The Lord of all the worlds is greater than anyone I stand before.
try: Before your next hard conversation, whisper that Allah is greater, then speak calmly.

title: Only the truth about Allah. Let my people go.
subtitle: Musa's duty and his demand
then: Musa told Firaun that {idea}it was a duty on him to say nothing about Allah but the truth{/idea}, and he had come with clear evidence. Then he asked for the Children of Israel: {reward}release them from your slavery and subjugation{/reward}, so they could worship their Lord.
now: You run the house, the team, the shop. Someone under you is stuck: overworked, unheard, afraid to ask. {trap}Their freedom is in your hands.{/trap} {idea}Speaking the truth about Allah includes loosening what you hold too tight.{/idea}
old: Faith is about what I believe, not how I treat those under me.
new: Truth about Allah comes with a call to free people from harm.
try: Ease one burden on someone who depends on you today: a day off, a lighter task, a kind word.

title: Show me proof, said the man who had decided already.
subtitle: Asking for evidence with the door already shut

row.title: Fir'awn
sub: bring a sign, if you are truthful

row.title: I want proof
sub: but I will not believe anyway

then: Musa stood before Fir'awn and his court and said he was a messenger from the Lord of all that exists. He asked for the Children of Israel to be freed. Ibn Kathir explains that Fir'awn had {trap}already refused to believe or grant the request{/trap}, and only demanded a sign to see if the claim held up.
now: Someone sends you a long, careful article that challenges a habit of yours. You type back: send me a source. They send three. You skim one and close the tab. {idea}The question was never about evidence.{/idea} It was about whether you were willing to move.
old: I just need more proof before I change anything.
new: Asking for proof only means something if I am ready to act on it.
try: Pick one thing you keep asking proof for. Ask yourself honestly: what would I do if I got it?

title: A plain staff became the sign no one could deny.
subtitle: The answer came in front of everyone
then: Fir'awn asked for a sign, and Musa threw down his staff. Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that it became a huge serpent that rushed toward Fir'awn, who {trap}jumped from his throne and cried to Musa for help{/trap}. The man who claimed to be lord could not hold his seat.
now: You walk into a meeting with someone who controls your contract. Their office, their rules, their tone. It all feels permanent. Then one email from above changes everything in a minute. {idea}What looks unshakable is held up by Allah, and can be moved by Him.{/idea}
old: The people with power over me are the ones really in control.
new: Every throne sits on ground that belongs to Allah.
try: Next time you feel small before someone powerful, quietly say: Allah is greater. Then speak calmly.

title: His hand came out shining, and not from sickness.
subtitle: A second sign, gentle and bright
then: After the staff, Musa drew his hand from his cloak and it shone white for the onlookers. Ibn Kathir notes, citing 27:12, that it was {idea}bright without any hurt{/idea}, not leprosy or disease. He put it back, and it returned to its usual color.
now: Some lessons come to you loud: a scare at the doctor, a lost job. Others come quiet: a stranger's kindness on a bad day, a line in a book at the right moment. {reward}Both are signs.{/reward} The quiet ones are easier to walk past.
old: Only dramatic moments count as a message from Allah.
new: Allah shows His signs in fear and in light, and both deserve attention.
try: Tonight, write down one small, gentle good thing from today that you almost missed.

title: When the truth was clear, they gave it a label.
subtitle: Calling it magic so they could ignore it
then: Once Fir'awn felt safe and returned to his throne, he told his chiefs this was a well-versed sorcerer, and they agreed. Ibn Kathir says they {trap}plotted to portray Musa as a liar and a fake{/trap}, to put out the light he brought.
now: A friend points out, kindly, that you snap at your kids when you are tired. You say: oh, she is just being dramatic. One word, and the point is gone. {trap}A label is a quick way to not listen.{/trap}
old: If I can name what is wrong with the messenger, I can ignore the message.
new: Dismissing the speaker does not make the truth go away.
try: Recall one piece of advice you dismissed by labeling the person. Think about the advice itself for two minutes.

title: They turned a call to worship into a threat to land.
subtitle: Fear of losing position, dressed up as defense
then: The chiefs told the people that Musa wanted to drive them out of their land through magic. Ibn Kathir says they feared he would win people over and prevail over them. Citing 28:6, he notes that {trap}what they feared is exactly what came to them{/trap}.
now: A new colleague suggests a fairer way to share the workload. Instead of asking if it is fair, you hear: they are after my role. You start talking about them in the break room. {idea}Fear of losing a position can make good advice sound like an attack.{/idea}
old: Anyone who changes things here is a threat to me.
new: Before I fight a change, I should check if I am only guarding my own place.
try: Think of one change at work or home you resisted. Ask: was it bad, or just bad for my ego?

title: Delay him, they said, and gather the experts.
subtitle: Buying time instead of facing the truth

row.title: it is the same trick
sub: we can beat it with ours

then: The chiefs advised Fir'awn to delay Musa and his brother and send gatherers through the provinces. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}magic was widespread and popular then{/trap}, and they wrongly assumed Musa's signs were the same kind of thing, so they could be beaten the same way.
now: A doctor tells you to change how you eat. You say, let me think about it, and start reading every article that says you are fine. {trap}Delay plus a search for the answer you want.{/trap} It feels like research. It is a way to avoid the decision.
old: I will wait and find someone who tells me otherwise.
new: Postponing the truth while I shop for opinions is still a refusal.
try: Name one thing you are putting off deciding. Set a date this week to decide it.

title: Every expert in the land, against one man and Allah.
subtitle: Gathering numbers to drown out the truth

row.title: one staff
sub: and the One who sent it

then: The plan was to bring every skilled sorcerer to Fir'awn. Ibn Kathir links this to 20:58-60, where Fir'awn set a meeting on a festival day in front of the people. {trap}He gathered his plot{/trap}, sure that numbers and skill would win.
now: You are the only one in the office who will not fudge the expense report. Everyone else has a reason, and there are more of them. It starts to feel like you are the strange one. {idea}How many agree has never been the measure of what is right.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me thinks it is fine, it must be fine.
new: A crowd of experts cannot make falsehood true.
try: Next time you are outnumbered on something you know is right, stay kind and stay put.

title: The first thing the magicians asked about was pay.
subtitle: Working for whoever pays, before the truth showed
then: The sorcerers came to Fir'awn, and before anything else they asked about their reward if they won. Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn {reward}promised them tremendous provisions{/reward} and made them hope for what they wished for. Their skill was for hire.
now: A client offers you a big bonus to write reviews for a product you have never used. The first question in your head is: how much? {trap}The question about right and wrong comes second, if at all.{/trap}
old: If the pay is good, the job is fine.
new: The first question about any work should be whether it is right, not what it pays.
try: Look at one task you do for money. Ask once, plainly: would I do this if it were seen by Allah? Then decide.

title: Yes, and you will be close to me, said Fir'awn.
subtitle: The lure of money and an inner circle
then: Fir'awn did not only promise money. Ibn Kathir explains he promised to make them {reward}among his private audience and best associates{/reward}. Status and closeness to power were the real hook.
now: Your boss hints you could join the leadership group if you back a decision you know is unfair. A seat at the table. Your name on the invite list. {trap}Belonging can be a stronger bribe than cash.{/trap}
old: Being close to the important people is worth a small compromise.
new: Closeness bought by betraying the truth is distance from Allah.
try: Notice one circle you want to be part of. Ask what it costs you to stay in it.

title: You throw first, or shall we? They came confident.
subtitle: The challenge on the festival day
then: On the appointed day, the magicians faced Musa and offered him the choice of who would throw first. Ibn Kathir notes that in 20:65 they offered to be the first. {trap}They were sure of their craft{/trap} and of the crowd watching.
now: You walk into an argument with your spouse fully loaded: dates, receipts, screenshots. You are certain you will win. {idea}Being prepared is not the same as being right.{/idea}
old: If I am skilled and prepared, I will win.
new: Skill used against the truth only delays the moment it loses.
try: Before your next disagreement, ask yourself first: what if I am the one who is wrong here?

title: They fooled the eyes, but the ropes were still ropes.
subtitle: A great show that was only an illusion
then: Musa told them to throw first. Ibn Kathir gives the wisdom: the people would see the sorcery first, so the truth would land harder when it came. Ibn 'Abbas said they threw ropes and sticks that {trap}appeared to crawl, an illusion{/trap} that struck terror into the crowd.
now: A feed full of perfect homes, perfect bodies, perfect marriages. Filters, angles, edits. You close the app feeling behind on everything. {trap}The ropes look like snakes.{/trap} {idea}Your eyes were played, but your life did not change.{/idea}
old: What I see on the screen is how things really are.
new: A great show can bewitch my eyes without being real.
try: Next time a post makes you feel less, say to yourself: rope, not snake. Then put the phone down.

title: One staff swallowed every lie they had thrown.
subtitle: Truth does not argue with illusion, it ends it
then: At that moment Allah inspired Musa to throw his staff. Ibn Ishaq said it {idea}followed the ropes and sticks one after another until nothing remained{/idea}, then became a staff again in his hand. The magicians knew this was not magic.
now: Your head is full of rope-snakes at 2am: they all think I am a failure, I will never fix this, it is too late. Then one true thought lands: Allah sees me and the door of repentance is open. {reward}One truth can swallow a dozen fears.{/reward}
old: There are too many problems for anything to fix them.
new: One truth from Allah outweighs any number of illusions.
try: Write down your loudest fear. Next to it, write one thing Allah says that answers it.

title: The truth stood, and all their work came to nothing.
subtitle: Effort spent against the truth is lost
then: The magicians had trained, traveled, and performed their best. In one moment, {idea}the truth was confirmed{/idea}, and {trap}all that they did was made of no effect{/trap}. Ibn Kathir calls it the moment Allah separated truth from falsehood.
now: Months spent building a cover story, keeping a version of yourself alive for people's approval. Then one honest conversation, and the whole structure falls. {trap}All that effort was for something that could not stand.{/trap}
old: If I put in enough effort, it will hold.
new: Only what is built on truth survives the moment truth appears.
try: Ask yourself which of your daily efforts would still matter if everything hidden were seen. Give that one more time.

title: Right there, in front of everyone, they were beaten.
subtitle: The festival meant to shame Musa shamed Fir'awn

row.title: Allah
sub: used it to show the truth

then: Fir'awn had chosen a festival day so the people could watch Musa fail. Instead, {trap}Fir'awn and his people were defeated there and returned humbled{/trap}. The crowd he gathered became witnesses against him.
now: You plan to show up a coworker in the big meeting, with slides ready to prove them wrong. The facts come out in their favor, in front of everyone you invited. {idea}Plans to humiliate others have a way of turning around.{/idea}
old: If I set it up right, I can make them look bad.
new: Whoever sets a stage against the truth ends up on it.
try: If you are planning to prove someone wrong in public, talk to them privately first.

title: The experts were the first to fall in prostration.
subtitle: Those who knew magic best recognized what was not
then: The magicians realized this was from heaven and by no means magic. Ibn Ishaq reports they said: had Musa been a magician, he would not have beaten us. {reward}They fell down prostrate{/reward}, the same people who had asked for a fee that morning.
now: You are the accountant who can tell when the numbers are real, the nurse who can tell when a patient is truly sick. {idea}Your expertise can lead you to the truth faster than anyone{/idea}, if you let it, instead of using it to hide.
old: What I know is just a skill I sell.
new: Real knowledge should bring me to my knees before Allah, not keep me standing proud.
try: In your field, notice one thing that shows Allah's design. Make a short sujud of thanks for it today.

title: We believe in the Lord of all the worlds.
subtitle: The magicians name the One above every throne
then: The magicians fell in prostration and proclaimed their belief in the Lord of all that exists. Ibn Kathir reports from Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazzah that {reward}they did not raise their heads before being shown Paradise and the Fire{/reward}. In front of the man who claimed to be their lord, they named a greater one.
now: You have worked for years to please one person: a parent, a boss, an audience. Their approval was your whole world. Then one day you see it clearly. {idea}They are one small part of a world Allah owns.{/idea} The weight shifts off your chest.
old: The person I answer to most is the biggest power in my life.
new: Allah is Lord of all the worlds, including everyone I fear or try to please.
try: In your next prayer, slow down at Rabbil alamin and think of the one person whose approval you chase.

title: The Lord of Musa and Harun, they made it unmistakable.
subtitle: Being specific so no one could twist their words

row.title: Lord of Musa and Harun
sub: the One these two called to

then: Fir'awn called himself lord of his people. So the magicians did not leave room for doubt: {idea}they believed in the Lord of Musa and Harun{/idea}. Ibn Ishaq reports they said that had Musa been a magician, he could not have beaten them.
now: At a family dinner someone mocks people who pray. You could mumble something about everyone believing in something. Or you could say, gently, {idea}I pray, and it matters to me.{/idea} Clarity is a kind of courage.
old: It is safer to keep my faith vague in public.
new: Real belief is willing to say whose side it is on.
try: Once this week, when your faith comes up, say plainly and kindly what you believe.

title: You believed before I gave you permission?
subtitle: A tyrant who wants to license even belief
then: Fir'awn accused the magicians of a plot with Musa. Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn knew it was false: Musa had never met them. He said it to {trap}deceive the ignorant masses{/trap}, citing 43:54: he fooled his people, and they obeyed him.
now: You quietly start praying again, and someone at home says: who told you to do that? Since when do you decide things without asking? {trap}Some people want a say even over your heart.{/trap} Your faith does not need their sign-off.
old: I need the approval of the people around me before I change.
new: No one has the right to give or withhold permission for my belief.
try: Think of one good change you are waiting for permission to make. Make a small start on it today.

title: When the argument was lost, he reached for threats.
subtitle: Cruelty is what is left when proof runs out
then: Fir'awn threatened the magicians with severe mutilation and crucifixion. Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that {trap}Fir'awn was the first to use these punishments{/trap}. He had lost the debate in front of everyone, so he turned to force.
now: In an argument you are losing, you feel the urge to raise your voice, bring up an old mistake, threaten to leave. {trap}That urge is the sign you have run out of reasons.{/trap} {idea}Notice it, and stop.{/idea}
old: If I cannot win the point, I can at least make them afraid.
new: Turning to threats is the clearest sign I have lost the argument.
try: Next time you feel like threatening or shouting, say: I need a minute. Then step away.

title: To our Lord we are returning, so do what you will.
subtitle: Remembering the return made the threat small
then: The magicians answered calmly that they were returning to their Lord. Ibn Kathir explains they meant: {idea}Allah's judgment is greater than yours{/idea}, so we will be patient with your punishment today. In 20:72 they told him: you can only decide for the life of this world.
now: Your manager threatens to block your promotion unless you sign off on numbers you know are false. Your stomach drops. Then you remember: {reward}one day I meet Allah, not this manager.{/reward} The threat is still real, but it gets smaller.
old: The person threatening me holds my future.
new: I am returning to Allah, and that puts every other threat in its place.
try: When something frightens you today, say quietly: inna ila rabbina munqalibun. Then breathe.

title: Our Lord, pour patience on us and let us die Muslim.
subtitle: The first prayer of new believers under threat

row.title: patience and a good end
sub: hold me firm to the last

then: The magicians told Fir'awn his only grievance was that they believed when the signs came. Then they prayed for patience and to die as Muslims. {reward}They started the day as sorcerers and ended it as martyrs{/reward}, as Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and others said.
now: A long illness, a hard marriage, a debt that will take years. You keep praying: take it away. Some days the better prayer is: {reward}pour patience on me, and let me end well.{/reward}
old: Faith means asking Allah to remove every hardship.
new: Sometimes the bravest prayer is for patience to carry it and a good end.
try: Add this to your dua today: Rabbana afrigh alayna sabran wa tawaffana muslimin.

title: The oppressors called the oppressed the mischief-makers.
subtitle: Fir'awn's chiefs push him to crush Bani Isra'il
then: The chiefs asked Fir'awn if he would let Musa and his people spread mischief. Ibn Kathir says: {trap}amazingly, they were worried Musa would cause mischief, when they were the mischief-makers{/trap}. Fir'awn renewed his order to kill the boys, and Ibn Kathir notes the opposite of what he intended came to pass.
now: At home, you are the one who slams doors, but you call your teenager the troublemaker when they finally push back. {trap}It is easy to name others as the problem.{/trap} {idea}Look first at who started the harm.{/idea}
old: The ones who disrupt my order are the problem.
new: Sometimes the order I am defending is the real corruption.
try: Think of someone you call difficult. Ask honestly what part of it you caused.

title: Seek help in Allah, be patient: the earth is His.
subtitle: Musa's advice to a frightened people
then: Fir'awn had just renewed his threat. Musa did not promise an easy road. He told his people to {idea}seek help in Allah and be patient{/idea}, because the earth belongs to Allah and {reward}the good end is for the righteous{/reward}.
now: Your landlord raises the rent again. The company is cutting jobs. It feels like other people own every piece of your life. {idea}The earth is Allah's.{/idea} Ask Him for help, do the next right thing, and wait well.
old: Whoever controls the ground controls my outcome.
new: The earth belongs to Allah, and the end belongs to those who fear Him.
try: Before you face something stressful today, make one short dua for help first, then act.

title: Harmed before you came, and harmed since you came.
subtitle: Tired believers, and the test that comes after relief

row.title: relief is a test
sub: He will see how you act

then: The Children of Israel told Musa they had suffered before he came and still suffered after. Musa answered that perhaps Allah would destroy their enemy and make them successors, {idea}so He may see how you act{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says he was encouraging them to be grateful when hardship is replaced by blessing.
now: For years you prayed for a stable job. Now you have it, the salary arrives every month. {idea}The question has changed.{/idea} It is no longer will Allah help me, but what am I doing with what He gave?
old: Once my problems are solved, the test is over.
new: Ease is its own test: Allah watches what I do with it.
try: Pick one blessing you prayed for in the past. Do one thing with it today that you would be glad Allah saw.

title: Hard years were sent so they might remember.
subtitle: Drought and shrinking harvests as a reminder
then: Allah tested Fir'awn's people with years of drought and poor harvests. Ibn Kathir reports from Raja' bin Haywah that {trap}a date palm would produce only one date{/trap}. The purpose is named in the verse: {idea}that they might remember{/idea}.
now: Business slows. The car breaks down the same week the boiler does. You curse your luck and scroll for distraction. {idea}A hard season can be an invitation{/idea} to stop and ask what Allah wants you to notice.
old: Hard times are just bad luck I have to get through.
new: Hardship can be a mercy meant to make me remember Allah.
try: Name one current difficulty. Ask: what is this reminding me of? Write one line.

title: Good times were ours; bad times were someone's fault.
subtitle: Taking credit for blessings, blaming others for trials

row.title: good season
sub: this is ours, we deserve it

row.title: good is mine, bad is yours

then: When good came, Fir'awn's people said it was theirs by right. When hardship came, they called Musa and his followers a bad omen. Ibn 'Abbas explained: {idea}their afflictions are with and from Allah{/idea}, but most of them did not know.
now: Your team hits the target: that was my strategy. The next quarter drops: the new hire slowed us down. {trap}Credit for me, blame for them.{/trap} The same pattern runs in families and marriages.
old: When things go well it is me, when they go badly it is someone else.
new: Both the good and the hard come from Allah, so I thank Him and look at myself.
try: Next time something goes wrong, before naming anyone, ask: what was my part?

title: Whatever sign you bring, we will not believe.
subtitle: A mind closed before the evidence arrives
then: Fir'awn's people told Musa that whatever sign he brought, they would call it sorcery and never believe. Ibn Kathir describes this as {trap}rebellion, defiance of the truth, and insistence on falsehood{/trap}. They closed the door before anyone knocked.
now: You have already decided your sister-in-law is selfish. She brings food when you are sick and you think: she just wants to look good. {trap}No act can reach you once the verdict is in.{/trap}
old: I have already made up my mind about this.
new: A heart that decides in advance cannot see any sign at all.
try: Pick one person you have a fixed opinion about. Look for one good thing they did this week.

title: Five clear signs, one after another, and still arrogance.
subtitle: Flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood
then: Allah sent the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood as distinct signs. Sa'id bin Jubayr describes how {idea}each one was removed when Musa prayed{/idea}, and each time they broke their promise. {trap}They remained arrogant{/trap}, a people set on wrongdoing.
now: The first warning from your doctor. Then the second. Then the test results. Each time you promise to change, and each time the fear fades and you go back. {idea}Every sign was also a door held open.{/idea}
old: One more warning and then I will change.
new: Every sign I ignore was a mercy that gave me another chance.
try: Name one warning you have had more than once. Take one concrete step on it today.

title: Remove this and we will believe, they promised every time.
subtitle: Promises made under pressure

row.title: a deal with Allah
sub: help me and I will change

then: When each punishment struck, they came to Musa: pray to your Lord, and if He removes this, we will believe and let the Children of Israel go. Ibn Ishaq describes the same {trap}promise made again and again{/trap} with each new sign.
now: In the hospital corridor waiting for news, you promise: if they are okay, I will pray every day. They recover. Two weeks later the prayer mat is folded away. {idea}A promise made in fear needs to be kept in ease.{/idea}
old: If Allah gets me out of this, then I will change.
new: The test of a promise made in hardship is what I do after relief.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Do one part of it today.

title: The moment relief came, they broke their word.
subtitle: A reprieve for a set term, and a broken promise

row.title: a set term
sub: time given to keep my word

then: Each time Musa prayed, Allah lifted the affliction for a fixed term. And each time, as Sa'id bin Jubayr describes, {trap}they did not believe and did not let the Children of Israel go{/trap}. Ibn Ishaq says this happened after the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood.
now: After the panic attack you swear you will stop working till 2am. The next week feels fine, and the laptop is open at midnight again. {idea}The relief was not the end of the story. It was the time given to keep the promise.{/idea}
old: Once the danger passes, I can go back to normal.
new: Relief is a deadline to keep my word, not a release from it.
try: Think of the last time Allah lifted a worry for you. Do one thing today that honors what you promised then.

title: Many warnings ignored, and then the sea closed.
subtitle: The end of Fir'awn and his army
then: After all the signs, Fir'awn and his soldiers chased Musa into the sea that Allah had parted. Ibn Kathir says that {trap}when they had all entered, the sea closed over them{/trap}. The verse gives the reason: they denied Allah's signs and were heedless of them.
now: Heedlessness is quiet. It is the reminder you swipe away, the Friday you skip, the warning in your own chest you talk over. {idea}No single moment feels like a choice.{/idea} The verse asks you to notice while the sea is still open.
old: Ignoring a few reminders is not a big deal.
new: Heedlessness, repeated, is what closes the door.
try: Today, when a reminder of Allah crosses your day, stop for ten seconds instead of moving past it.

title: The oppressed inherited the land because they endured.
subtitle: Patience fulfilled a promise; pride lost its buildings
then: Allah gave the people who were considered weak the blessed land, which Al-Hasan and Qatadah said was Sham. {reward}The good word of your Lord was fulfilled because of their endurance.{/reward} Ibn Kathir links this to 28:5-6. And all that Fir'awn built and grew was destroyed.
now: You are the junior at work who does honest work while others take shortcuts and get noticed. You stay patient for years. {reward}Patience is not doing nothing.{/reward} It is holding steady while Allah's promise ripens.
old: The strong always win in the end.
new: Allah's promise is fulfilled for those who endure, and pride's buildings do not last.
try: Name one situation where you are holding on patiently. Ask Allah today to accept your sabr.

title: Just saved by a miracle, they asked for an idol.
subtitle: Wanting what the neighbors have, right after the sea

row.title: be like them
sub: they have one, so should we

then: Having just crossed the sea, the Children of Israel passed a people devoted to idols, which Ibn Jarir said were shaped like cows. They asked Musa for a god like theirs. Ibn Kathir cites a hadith: on the way to Hunayn, some new Muslims asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sacred tree like the pagans had. He said: {trap}you said just what the people of Musa said{/trap}.
now: Your friends all have a lucky charm, a horoscope app, a thing they touch before an exam. You start to want one too, just in case. {idea}The pull to copy what others hold sacred is old and strong.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me has it, it cannot be that bad.
new: Copying others' devotion right after Allah has saved me is forgetting who saved me.
try: Notice one habit you picked up only because others do it. Ask if it pulls you toward Allah or away.

title: What they worship will perish, and their work is in vain.
subtitle: Musa explains why the idols are worth nothing
then: Musa told his people that the idol worshippers they admired {trap}would perish in what they were doing{/trap}, and that all their work was in vain. Ibn Kathir says Musa was correcting their ignorance of Allah's greatness and His purity from any partner.
now: You see people giving their whole lives to a career, a team, an image. They are so devoted it looks admirable. {idea}Devotion is only as valuable as what it is aimed at.{/idea}
old: Anyone that devoted must be onto something.
new: Devotion aimed at anything other than Allah ends in nothing.
try: Look at where most of your energy went this week. Redirect ten minutes of it to Allah today.

title: Shall I seek a god other than Allah, who honored you?
subtitle: Musa reminds them what Allah already gave
then: Musa asked them: shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, when He has given you superiority over the nations? Ibn Kathir says he {reward}reminded them of Allah's blessings{/reward}, saving them from Fir'awn's tyranny and humiliation.
now: You have a home, health, a family that calls. Then a new phone comes out and you feel empty without it. {reward}Remembering what Allah has already given{/reward} makes the craving much smaller.
old: Something is missing, so I need something new.
new: When I remember what Allah gave me, I stop looking elsewhere to fill the gap.
try: List five things Allah has given you that you did not earn. Read the list once tonight.

title: Remember the worst days He brought you out of.
subtitle: Rescue from Fir'awn, and the trial within it
then: Allah reminds the Children of Israel how He saved them from Fir'awn's people, who {trap}killed their sons and kept their women alive{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says Musa reminded them of this to show what Allah had done, and the verse calls it {idea}a great trial from your Lord{/idea}.
now: You forget the year you could not pay rent, the night in the emergency room, the season of feeling completely alone. Life is easier now and you grumble about small things. {reward}Remembering the rescue{/reward} puts today in its place.
old: The hard years are behind me, better not to think about them.
new: Remembering where Allah brought me from keeps me grateful and humble.
try: Think of one hard time Allah brought you through. Say alhamdulillah for it specifically.

title: Forty nights alone with his Lord, and a trust left behind.
subtitle: Musa's appointment, and Harun left in charge
then: Allah appointed thirty nights for Musa and added ten. Ibn Kathir says scholars mention {idea}Musa fasted this period{/idea}, before receiving the Tawrah. He left his brother Harun with the people and told him to act rightly. Ibn Kathir notes this was only a reminder, since Harun was a noble prophet himself.
now: You hand your team to a colleague while you go on leave. Or you leave the kids with your sibling for a weekend. {idea}A short, clear reminder of what matters{/idea} is not distrust. It is care.
old: Reminding someone good feels like I do not trust them.
new: Even the best people benefit from a gentle reminder to do right.
try: Before handing something over this week, give one short reminder of what matters most, kindly.

title: The mountain could not bear it, and Musa fell.
subtitle: Longing to see Allah, and learning one's limits
then: Allah spoke to Musa directly, and Musa asked to see Him. Allah said he could not, and to look at the mountain. When Allah manifested to it, it collapsed to dust and Musa fell unconscious. Ibn Kathir notes that {reward}believers will see Allah in the Hereafter{/reward}, citing 75:22-23. Musa woke saying {idea}Glory be to You, I turn to You{/idea}.
now: Sometimes your heart wants more than this life can hold: certainty, closeness, answers. The longing is not wrong. {idea}Musa's answer was praise and turning back{/idea}, trusting that what is not given here is kept for later.
old: If I cannot have it now, it must not be meant for me.
new: Some things are too great for this world, and Allah keeps them for the next.
try: When you feel a longing you cannot satisfy, say subhanak and make dua for Jannah.

title: Take what I gave you, and be among the grateful.
subtitle: Chosen with a message, told to hold it and thank
then: Right after Musa asked to see Allah, he was told he had been chosen by Allah's messages and speech. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}hold to what I have given you and be grateful{/idea}, and do not ask for what is beyond your capacity to bear.
now: You keep thinking about the house you do not have, the talent you wish you had. Meanwhile you have a Quran on your phone, two hands, a quiet hour each morning. {reward}Take what you were given, and thank Him for it.{/reward}
old: I will be grateful when I get what I am hoping for.
new: Gratitude starts with holding firmly to what I already have.
try: Pick one gift you already have. Use it well today, and thank Allah for it out loud.

title: Hold it with strength, and take the best of it.
subtitle: The Tablets, given to be lived firmly
then: Allah wrote for Musa on the Tablets exhortation and explanation for all things. Ibn Kathir explains {idea}hold unto these with firmness{/idea} as being firm in obedience. He was to tell his people to take the best of it, and was warned he would see the home of the rebellious.
now: You read an ayah that moves you on Friday. By Monday it is gone, lost between emails and errands. {idea}Taking it with strength{/idea} means picking one thing from it and holding it all week.
old: I read it, so I have taken it.
new: Guidance is meant to be held with strength, not glanced at.
try: Choose one line of the Quran today. Write it somewhere you will see it every day this week.

title: Arrogance blinds a person to every sign.
subtitle: Seeing the right path and choosing the wrong one

row.title: lack of proof
sub: what I think the problem is

then: Allah says He will turn away from His signs those who are arrogant without right. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}just as they acted proudly without justification, Allah let them be disgraced with ignorance{/trap}. Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah said it means losing understanding of the Quran, and Ibn Kathir notes this applies in every nation.
now: Your spouse is right about something and you know it. But admitting it feels like losing, so you double down. {trap}Pride makes the wrong path look easier than the right one.{/trap} The more you do it, the harder it is to see.
old: I would change if someone showed me I was wrong.
new: Arrogance makes me blind to the very signs that would guide me.
try: Today, say I was wrong about one small thing to someone who deserves to hear it.

title: Deeds without faith in the meeting come to nothing.
subtitle: Each person is repaid for what they did

row.title: what I do
sub: good for good, evil for evil

then: Those who deny Allah's signs and the meeting in the Hereafter find their deeds made void. Ibn Kathir explains it as recompense matching action: {idea}good for good and evil for evil. As you sow, you reap.{/idea}
now: You plant tomatoes in the spring and you get tomatoes in summer, not roses. Every word to your kids, every hour at work, every choice in private is a seed. {reward}The harvest will match what you planted.{/reward}
old: What happens in the end is out of my hands.
new: I will be repaid for exactly what I did, so I can plant better today.
try: Do one good deed today with the meeting with Allah in mind, quietly, for Him alone.

title: A calf of their own gold that could not say a word.
subtitle: Worshipping what they made with their own hands
then: While Musa was at his appointment, As-Samiri made a calf from the ornaments the people had borrowed, and it seemed to low. Ibn Kathir says people {trap}danced around it and said this is your god and the god of Musa{/trap}. The verse asks: did they not see it could neither speak to them nor guide them?
now: Your salary, your follower count, your reputation. You built them with your own effort, and now they set your mood each morning. {trap}They make a lot of noise.{/trap} {idea}But not one of them can tell you how to live or carry you through death.{/idea}
old: What I built with my own hands is what I can depend on.
new: Anything that cannot guide me does not deserve my devotion, however much it shines.
try: Name one thing you made that you now serve. Spend today using it, not obeying it.

title: When regret came, they said: without His mercy we are lost.
subtitle: The first honest step back
then: After worshipping the calf, the people felt deep regret and saw they had gone astray. They said that if their Lord did not have mercy on them and forgive them, they would be lost. Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}their recognition of their sin and their way of seeking salvation from Allah{/reward}.
now: You wake up the morning after saying something cruel. The shame sits heavy. You can spiral into how bad you are, or you can say: {reward}Ya Allah, I was wrong, forgive me.{/reward} One leads nowhere. The other leads back.
old: After what I did, there is no point asking.
new: Regret is meant to turn me toward Allah's mercy, not away from it.
try: Think of one thing you regret. Say this verse's words as a dua: if You do not forgive me, I am lost.

title: Seeing it with his own eyes, Musa threw down the Tablets.
subtitle: Anger for Allah's sake, and a brother's plea
then: Musa returned angry and grieved. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}information is not like seeing{/idea}. Allah had told Musa about the calf, but he only threw the Tablets when he saw it. He grabbed Harun, fearing he had not tried hard enough. Harun said: {trap}the people overpowered me and almost killed me{/trap}.
now: You come home and the kitchen is a mess, the kids are on screens, and you turn on your partner before asking a single question. {idea}Anger for the right reason can still land on the wrong person.{/idea} Hear their side first.
old: When I am angry for a good reason, I am allowed to react.
new: Even righteous anger needs to listen before it blames.
try: Next time you walk into a situation that angers you, ask one question before you say anything else.

title: Forgive me and my brother, Most Merciful of the merciful.
subtitle: Musa's first words after his anger cooled

row.title: pray for us both
sub: me and the one I hurt

then: When Musa was satisfied his brother was innocent, Ibn Kathir says, citing 20:90, that Harun had warned the people they were being tested. Musa then prayed: {reward}My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy{/reward}. He began with himself.
now: After a heated fight with your sibling, you find out they were not to blame. You could quietly move on. Or you could say sorry, and in your sujud that night ask Allah to {reward}forgive you both{/reward}.
old: Once I find out I was wrong, it is easier to just drop it.
new: Repair starts with asking forgiveness for myself and praying for the one I hurt.
try: Make dua tonight for someone you were harsh with recently. Name them in it.

title: Inventing falsehood about Allah carries its own disgrace.
subtitle: The consequence of the calf, and of every invented lie
then: The verse says those who took the calf would meet anger from their Lord and humiliation in this life. Abu Qilabah said: {idea}by Allah, this ayah is for all who invent a lie, until the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah said every person who invents in religion will taste disgrace.
now: It is easy to make up a rule about religion that suits your mood, or to repeat something as from the Prophet ﷺ without checking. {trap}Inventing about Allah is heavy.{/trap} {idea}Saying I do not know is safer.{/idea}
old: It is fine to say what I think religion means, it is just my opinion.
new: Speaking about Allah without knowledge is serious, so I check before I speak.
try: Before you forward the next religious quote, check its source first. If you cannot, do not send it.

title: Whatever you did, after repentance your Lord forgives.
subtitle: The door that stays open, even after the calf
then: Right after the warning about the calf comes this promise. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah accepts repentance for any sin, even shirk, disbelief and hypocrisy{/reward}. He notes the verse addresses the Prophet ﷺ, the messenger of repentance and mercy.
now: You have a list in your head of things you did that you think Allah could never let go: the years without prayer, the lies, the person you hurt. {reward}The verse says: after all that, your Lord is Forgiving.{/reward} The word after matters.
old: Some things I did are too big for Allah to forgive.
new: No sin is bigger than Allah's forgiveness for someone who turns back.
try: Pray two rak'ahs tonight with the intention of repentance. Ask for one specific thing to be forgiven.

title: When his anger quieted, Musa picked the Tablets back up.
subtitle: Guidance and mercy, waiting after the storm
then: Musa had thrown the Tablets out of anger for Allah's sake. When the anger subsided, {idea}he took them up again{/idea}. In them was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord. Ibn Kathir mentions reports that they had broken, adding that only Allah knows if those reports are true.
now: You slammed the Quran app shut after a bad day, or stopped praying for a week after an argument. The anger has passed now. {reward}The guidance is still there, waiting for you to pick it up.{/reward}
old: I dropped it in a bad moment, so I have lost it.
new: When the anger settles, I can pick up guidance again and find mercy in it.
try: If you put down a good habit in a hard moment, pick it back up today, in a small way.

title: You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy.
subtitle: Musa's plea when the seventy were struck
then: Musa took seventy men to the appointment to seek forgiveness for the calf. Reports in Ibn Kathir say they demanded to see Allah, or did not forbid their people. {trap}They were seized by a tremor.{/trap} Musa did not argue. He said this was {idea}Allah's trial{/idea}, and asked: You are our Protector, so forgive us.
now: Something hits your whole family at once: a layoff, a diagnosis, a loss. You want to ask why us. {idea}Musa's words show another way{/idea}: this is a test, You are in charge, You are our Wali, forgive and have mercy on us.
old: When something bad hits us, it means Allah has turned against us.
new: A trial is from Allah, and the answer is to turn to Him as our Protector.
try: In your next dua, say: Anta waliyyuna faghfir lana warhamna. Mean it for your whole household.

title: My mercy embraces all things, says Allah.
subtitle: Asking for good in both worlds, and the answer
then: Musa asked Allah for good in this world and the next, saying: we have turned back to You. Ibn Kathir says hudna means {idea}we repent and return to You{/idea}. Allah replied that His {reward}mercy embraces all things{/reward}, and He will write it for those who are mindful of Him, give zakah, and believe in His signs.
now: You are in the waiting room, scared, feeling like you have no right to ask for anything. {reward}Mercy that covers everything covers this room too.{/reward} Ask for the good of this life and the next, and turn back to Him while you ask.
old: Allah's mercy is for people better than me.
new: His mercy covers all things, and I can step into it by turning back to Him.
try: Say this dua today: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah wa fil-akhirati hasanah.

title: The Prophet ﷺ came to lift the heavy burdens.
subtitle: Mercy written for those who follow the unlettered Prophet
then: This answers who the mercy of 7:156 is for: those who follow the unlettered Prophet ﷺ, described in earlier scriptures. Ibn Kathir says {reward}he came with leniency and an easy religion{/reward}, citing his words: I was sent with the easy way of pure monotheism, and his advice to make things easy, not difficult.
now: Maybe you feel religion as a list you keep failing. Too many rules, too much guilt. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ was sent to take shackles off, not add them.{/reward} Following him starts with that lightness.
old: Being religious means carrying a heavy load.
new: Following the Prophet ﷺ is a release from heavy burdens, not a new one.
try: Next time someone asks you about Islam, share one thing that makes life easier, not harder.

title: I am the Messenger of Allah to you all.
subtitle: A message for every person, everywhere
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say he is Allah's Messenger to all people. Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}directed to mankind, red and black, Arab and non-Arab alike{/idea}. He cites Abu Bakr's moment: when others said you lie, Abu Bakr said you speak the truth.
now: You sometimes feel the message is for the people at the masjid who know Arabic, who grew up with it. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ said: to you all.{/idea} That includes you on your commute, at your desk, wherever you are.
old: This message is for people more religious than me.
new: The Prophet ﷺ was sent to me as much as to anyone.
try: Read one hadith today as if the Prophet ﷺ were saying it directly to you.

title: Among them was a group who guided by truth.
subtitle: In the middle of the failures, the faithful are named
then: After the story of the calf, the Quran pauses to say that among the people of Musa {reward}is a community who guide by truth and establish justice{/reward}. Ibn Kathir links this to 3:113 and 3:199, which describe people of earlier scripture who stand in prayer at night and humble themselves before Allah.
now: When a family, a team or a neighborhood has let you down, it is easy to write off everyone in it. {idea}The Quran does not do that.{/idea} Even in the hardest story, it stops to honor the ones who stayed true.
old: Once a group has failed, everyone in it is the same.
new: Justice means seeing the upright people even among those who went wrong.
try: Think of a group you have written off. Name one person in it who does good, and say something kind about them.

title: Twelve springs from one rock, and shade, and food.
subtitle: Every need provided, and still they wronged themselves

picture.label: What was given in the desert

then: Allah divided the Children of Israel into twelve tribes. When they asked for water, Musa struck a rock and twelve springs burst out, {reward}each group knowing its own place{/reward}. Clouds shaded them and manna and quails fed them. The verse closes: {trap}they did not wrong Us, they wronged themselves{/trap}.
now: You have running water, a fridge with food, a roof when it rains. Then you skip prayer, snap at your mother, scroll past midnight. {trap}None of it harms Allah.{/trap} It only takes from the person you could have been.
old: When I disobey, I am pushing against Allah.
new: Allah gave me everything, and my sins only hurt me.
try: Drink your next glass of water slowly and say bismillah and alhamdulillah for it.

title: Enter humbly, ask forgiveness, and it is yours.
subtitle: A simple instruction at the gate of the city
then: The Children of Israel were told to settle in the city, eat freely, and {idea}enter the gate humbly, asking forgiveness{/idea}. Allah promised to forgive them and increase the doers of good. Ibn Kathir notes this was revealed in Makkah and also discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
now: You get the keys to a new apartment, or walk into the first day of a new job. The moment you cross the threshold is a chance. {idea}Walk in saying astaghfirullah and alhamdulillah{/idea}, not just I made it.
old: A new start is something I earned.
new: Every new door is to be entered humbly, asking Allah's forgiveness.
try: The next time you enter your home today, say astaghfirullah once as you step in.

title: They were given a word and changed it.
subtitle: Swapping a simple command for their own version
then: Those who did wrong among them {trap}changed the word that had been told to them{/trap}. Instead of the humble request for forgiveness, they said something else. So a punishment came from the sky for the wrong they were doing.
now: Your parent asks you to apologize to your sister. You say sorry you feel that way. The words are close, but the meaning is gone. {trap}Changing the instruction while pretending to follow it{/trap} is still disobedience.
old: As long as I do something close to what was asked, it counts.
new: Twisting a clear instruction into my own version is a quiet refusal.
try: Pick one thing you were asked to do, by Allah or a person you owe. Do it exactly as asked today.

title: The fish came on the one day they were told to stop.
subtitle: A test, and a clever trick to get around it
then: The town was Aylah, by the sea, according to Ibn 'Abbas. On the day they were forbidden to fish, the fish came openly; on other days, they did not. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they used a trick, an action that seemed legal on the surface{/trap}, to break Allah's command. The verse calls it a test.
now: You would never steal. But you can claim the expense that is technically allowed. You would never lie. But you can word the email so they draw the wrong conclusion. {trap}A loophole is still a choice.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees the intent.{/idea}
old: If it is technically allowed, it is fine.
new: Tricks around Allah's limits fail, because He sees what I meant.
try: Think of one loophole you use. Ask: if I explained my reason to Allah, would I be comfortable?

title: Why bother warning them? So we are excused before Allah.
subtitle: Three groups in the town, and the reason to keep speaking
then: Ibn Kathir says the town split into three: those who broke the rule, those who warned them, and those who did neither. The silent group asked why bother. The advisers answered: {idea}to be free of blame before your Lord, and perhaps they may fear Him{/idea}.
now: Your friend is getting into gambling, or a cousin keeps drinking and driving. Everyone says: they will not listen, leave it. {idea}You do not speak because you are sure it will work.{/idea} You speak because it is right, and because maybe it will.
old: If they will not listen, there is no point saying anything.
new: I give sincere advice to be clear before Allah, and in hope they may change.
try: Think of one person you have stopped advising. Send one short, kind message today.

title: Those who forbade evil were saved.
subtitle: When the reminder was forgotten, the outcome divided
then: When the wrongdoers ignored the reminder, Allah {reward}rescued those who forbade evil{/reward} and seized the wrongdoers. Ibn Kathir notes the silent group is not mentioned. Ikrimah persuaded Ibn 'Abbas that they too were saved, and Ibn 'Abbas gave him a garment for it.
now: Staying out of it can feel like the safe middle. Not part of the wrong, not making waves. {reward}The verse names the ones who spoke up as the ones saved.{/reward} Silence is not as safe as it looks.
old: If I do not join in, I have done my part.
new: Gently standing against wrong is what the verse holds up as saving.
try: When you hear gossip or a cruel joke today, gently change the subject or say that is not fair.

title: When they kept pushing past the limit, they were humbled.
subtitle: The end of those who mocked the boundary
then: When the Sabbath-breakers {trap}went arrogantly beyond what they were forbidden{/trap}, Allah said: be apes, despised. Ibn Kathir explains despised as humiliated and rejected. It came after the trick, the warnings and the forgetting.
now: It starts with one late night, one small lie, one glance you should not take. Then the limit stops feeling like a limit. {idea}The time to stop is while it is still small.{/idea}
old: I can push the line a bit and still come back.
new: Each step past Allah's limit makes the next one easier, so I stop early.
try: Name one line you have been slowly pushing. Step back from it today, even a little.

title: Swift in penalty, and Forgiving, Merciful, in one breath.
subtitle: Warning and hope placed side by side
then: Allah declared that those who kept defying His law and using tricks around it would face hardship until the Day of Resurrection. Then the verse ends: your Lord is swift in penalty, and He is Forgiving, Merciful. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah mentions warning and encouragement together so hearts always have hope and fear{/idea}.
now: You might live only on fear: every mistake feels like the end. Or only on hope: nothing you do really matters. {idea}This verse holds both.{/idea} Take sin seriously, and never stop believing He forgives.
old: Either Allah is strict with me, or He is merciful, not both.
new: Allah's justice keeps me careful, and His mercy keeps me from despair.
try: Tonight, name one sin to stay away from and one hope to hold on to.

title: Tested with good and bad, so they might return.
subtitle: Some righteous, some not, and every season a test
then: Allah scattered the Children of Israel into groups, {reward}some righteous{/reward} and some less so. Ibn Kathir says Allah tested them with ease and difficulty, eagerness and fear, well-being and affliction, {idea}so they might turn back to Him{/idea}.
now: A promotion one year, a miscarriage the next. A good scan, then a bad one. {idea}Both seasons carry the same question:{/idea} will this bring me closer to Allah, or further away?
old: Good times mean Allah is pleased, bad times mean He is not.
new: Good and bad are both tests meant to bring me back to Allah.
try: Whatever kind of day you are having, end it with two minutes of quiet dhikr.

title: They grabbed the quick gain and said: we will be forgiven.
subtitle: Sinning on a promise of forgiveness never asked for
then: A later generation inherited the Book and studied it, but {trap}took whatever this low life offered and said: we will be forgiven{/trap}. As-Suddi described judges who took bribes, saying this. Ibn 'Abbas said the covenant they broke included claiming Allah will forgive sins they keep committing without repenting.
now: You know the rule. You break it anyway and tell yourself Allah is Merciful, I will sort it out later. Then the chance comes again, and you take it again. {idea}The home of the Hereafter is better{/idea}, the verse says. Do you not think?
old: Allah is Merciful, so I can keep doing it and ask later.
new: Hoping for forgiveness while planning to repeat the sin is fooling myself.
try: Name one sin you keep excusing with Allah is Merciful. Today, stop once and actually repent.

title: Hold fast to the Book, keep the prayer, nothing is wasted.
subtitle: The reformers whose reward is never lost
then: After describing those who took quick gain, Allah praises the opposite. Ibn Kathir says these are people who {idea}adhere to the Book, follow its commands, avoid its prohibitions{/idea}, and keep the prayer. {reward}Their reward will not be lost.{/reward}
now: Some days you pray quickly and tiredly, read one ayah and close the app. It feels like nothing. {reward}Allah says He does not waste the reward of those who keep at it.{/reward}
old: My small, tired efforts do not count for much.
new: Allah keeps the reward of everyone who holds on to His Book and prayer.
try: Pray your next salah on time, even if it is short. Trust that it is kept.

title: With the mountain overhead, they were told: hold on firmly.
subtitle: A covenant taken with the mountain raised above them
then: Ibn 'Abbas said that when Musa brought the Tablets, {trap}the commands felt heavy and the people did not want to follow them{/trap}. So the mountain was raised over them like a canopy, and they were told to {idea}hold firmly to what was given and remember what is in it{/idea}.
now: You know what you need to change. It feels heavy, so you keep putting it off. Then a scare comes, a lump, a near miss on the motorway, and suddenly it is clear. {idea}Hold on to it now, before the mountain is overhead.{/idea}
old: I will take my faith seriously when I really have to.
new: Guidance is meant to be taken with strength now, not only in a crisis.
try: Choose one teaching you have found heavy. Take one firm step on it today, before life forces you.

title: Am I not your Lord? Every soul once answered yes.
subtitle: The covenant taken before anyone was born

row.title: Yes, we testify
sub: so no one can say I forgot

then: Allah brought Adam's descendants out and made them testify that He is their Lord. Ibn Kathir links this to the fitrah in 30:30 and the hadith that {idea}every child is born upon the fitrah{/idea}. The reason is given: so no one can say on the Day of Resurrection, we were unaware.
now: Sometimes, in a quiet moment, on a night drive or holding a newborn, something in you reaches for Allah without being taught. {reward}That pull is the old yes.{/reward} It was there before any lesson.
old: Faith is something I have to build from nothing.
new: I already said yes to Allah once, and my heart remembers.
try: Sit for one quiet minute tonight and say: Bala, You are my Lord.

title: Our fathers did it is not an excuse.
subtitle: Inherited habits do not cancel your own covenant

row.title: we just followed
sub: will You punish us for them?

row.title: my upbringing
sub: it is how I was raised

then: The covenant was taken so people could not say on the Day: {trap}it was our fathers who took partners with Allah, we were only their descendants{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says each person testified for themselves, so the excuse of following the elders falls away.
now: My family always did it this way. Everyone in my town does it. It is cultural. These are real pressures. {idea}But each of us said our own yes{/idea}, and each of us answers for our own choices.
old: I cannot be blamed for what I was raised with.
new: My upbringing explains me, but I still answer for my own choices.
try: Name one habit you inherited. Ask honestly: would I choose this if I were starting fresh?

title: The signs are spelled out so that they might return.
subtitle: Detail given for one purpose: coming back
then: After reminding people of the covenant, Allah says: thus do We explain the verses in detail, {idea}so that they may turn back{/idea}. The long stories of this surah all serve this purpose: to bring people back to the yes they once gave.
now: You have read this surah's stories before: Fir'awn, the calf, the Sabbath town. Easy to treat them as history. {idea}They are written so you return.{/idea} Each one is a door back home.
old: These stories are about people long ago.
new: Every detail Allah explains is an invitation for me to return.
try: Pick one story from this surah. Ask: where is the way back for me in it?

title: Given the signs, he slipped out of them like a skin.
subtitle: A man of knowledge who walked away from it

row.title: I know, so I am safe

then: Ibn Mas'ud and others said this is about Bal'am bin Ba'ura, a man given knowledge of Allah's signs. Malik bin Dinar reported that {trap}a king gave him land and gifts, and he left the religion of Musa{/trap}. Ibn 'Abbas said his people kept pressing him to pray against Musa until he did.
now: You know the hadiths. You can quote the ayat. Then a job offer comes that needs you to bend one rule, and then another. {trap}Knowledge does not protect you by itself.{/trap} It can be peeled off, one gift at a time.
old: Because I know so much about the deen, I am safe.
new: Knowledge I do not live by can be stripped away.
try: Take one thing you know well about Islam. Act on it today, in a way no one sees.

title: He could have been raised, but he clung to the ground.
subtitle: The parable of the panting dog
then: Allah could have raised him by those signs, {trap}but he clung to the earth and followed his desires{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says he was drawn by the adornment of this life. One meaning of the parable: like a dog that pants whether chased or left alone, {trap}advice never reached him{/trap}. The verse ends: relate the stories, perhaps they will think.
now: A raise, then a bigger car, then a bigger house, and the restlessness never stops. Push yourself or rest, it is the same breathless feeling. {idea}Clinging to the ground keeps you panting.{/idea}
old: Once I get a bit more, I will finally feel settled.
new: Clinging to this world keeps me restless whatever I get.
try: Skip one purchase or upgrade you were planning this week. Notice how it feels.

title: An evil example, and the harm landed on themselves.
subtitle: The ones who rejected the signs wronged only their own souls
then: The verse closes the story of the man who abandoned Allah's signs. {trap}How evil is the example of those who reject the signs{/trap}, and the verse says it plainly: {trap}they used to wrong themselves{/trap}.
now: You stop praying, skip the Quran, drift away from the mosque friends. Allah is not smaller for it. {trap}You are.{/trap} The restlessness, the shorter temper, the empty Sunday evenings: that is the cost, and you are the one paying it.
old: Leaving the deen only matters to religious people.
new: Turning from Allah's signs only wrongs my own soul.
try: Bring back one small act of worship you dropped. Do it once today.

title: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided.
subtitle: Guidance is His to give, so ask Him for it
then: After the story of a learned man who lost his way, the verse says whom Allah guides is the guided one. Ibn Kathir cites the opening words the Prophet ﷺ used, reported by Ibn Mas'ud: {idea}whom Allah guides, none can mislead; whom He misguides, none can guide{/idea}.
now: You have read the books, watched the lectures, argued the points. Still you know people smarter than you who drifted away. {idea}Guidance is not a skill you master.{/idea} It is a gift you keep asking for, seventeen times a day in al-Fatiha.
old: If I learn enough, I will stay on the right path.
new: Guidance is Allah's gift, so I keep asking for it humbly.
try: In your next prayer, say ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim slowly and mean it as a request.

title: Hearts that do not understand, eyes that do not see.
subtitle: Having senses and not using them for guidance
then: The verse speaks soberly of those headed for Hell: they have hearts, eyes and ears they do not use for guidance. Ibn Kathir cites 22:46: {trap}it is not the eyes that grow blind, but the hearts in the chests{/trap}. Cattle at least answer their shepherd's call; these did not.
now: You watched three hours of videos today and heard nothing that moved you. Your eyes passed over the sunset and saw only traffic. {idea}The senses work fine.{/idea} The question is whether they are taking anything in for the heart.
old: I see and hear everything around me.
new: My senses were given to lead me to Allah, not just to fill my day.
try: Today, look at one thing in nature for one full minute and think of who made it.

title: To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call Him by them.
subtitle: Calling on Allah by the names that fit your need
then: Allah's names are the most beautiful, and believers are told to call Him by them. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ teaching a dua for grief that asks Allah {reward}by every name He has{/reward}. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said deviating in His names included naming idols like Al-Lat from Allah's name.
now: You are sitting in the hospital car park. Instead of just please, you say: {reward}Ya Shafi, Ya Rahim.{/reward} Lost money: Ya Razzaq. A wrong you did: Ya Ghafur. Each name is a door matched to the need.
old: Dua is just asking for what I want.
new: Calling Allah by the name that fits my need makes my dua more alive.
try: Pick one name of Allah that fits your biggest worry. Use it in your dua tonight.

title: There will always be some who guide by truth.
subtitle: A community that keeps to truth and justice
then: After describing the heedless, Allah says there is a community that guides by truth and establishes justice. Ibn Kathir notes reports that this refers to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, and cites the hadith: {reward}there will always be a group of my Ummah apparent on the truth, unharmed by those who oppose them{/reward}.
now: After reading the news, it can feel like everyone has lost their way. {reward}But somewhere a teacher is staying late for a struggling student. A judge is refusing a bribe.{/reward} Look for them, and try to be one.
old: Everyone is corrupt, so what difference can I make?
new: There are always people standing on truth, and I can be among them.
try: Find one person living with integrity near you. Thank them, or learn from them, this week.

title: Step by step, led on from where they do not notice.
subtitle: When ease becomes a trap

row.title: Allah is pleased
sub: look how well I am doing

then: Those who reject Allah's signs are led on gradually from where they do not perceive. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}the doors of provision are opened for them, and they are deceived into thinking they are on the right path{/trap}. He cites 6:44, where the gates of everything opened just before the end.
now: You stopped praying months ago, and since then work has gone great: the promotion, the bonus, the new flat. It is tempting to think it does not matter. {idea}Success while far from Allah is not a sign of His approval.{/idea}
old: If life is going well, I must be doing something right.
new: Ease while I ignore Allah may be drawing me further away, step by step.
try: On your next good day, check yourself: am I closer to Allah than last month, or further?

title: I give them time, and My plan is firm.
subtitle: Delay is not escape
then: Following the last verse, Allah says He gives them time, and {idea}His plan is firm{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains it as prolonging what they are in, while the plan stays strong and perfect.
now: You did something wrong years ago and nothing came of it. It is easy to forget it, as if it never happened. {idea}The time you have been given is not proof you got away.{/idea} {reward}It is the space to turn back.{/reward}
old: Nothing bad happened, so it must not have mattered.
new: Allah's respite is time given to repent, not proof I escaped.
try: Think of an old wrong you have never repented from. Repent today, and fix what you can.

title: Your companion is not mad, he is a clear warner.
subtitle: Think honestly about the man you have known for years
then: Qatadah reports that the Prophet ﷺ stood on As-Safa and called the clans of Quraysh one by one, warning them. Some said: {trap}this companion of yours is mad{/trap}. The verse came: do they not reflect? Ibn Kathir links it to 34:46: {idea}stand for Allah in pairs or alone, and think{/idea}.
now: Someone you have known for years, honest in everything, tells you a hard truth. Your first reaction: they have gone crazy, they are being extreme. {idea}Stop and think about who is saying it.{/idea} The person, not the label.
old: If a message makes me uncomfortable, the messenger must be unbalanced.
new: Honest reflection on the messenger's character shows the truth of the message.
try: Spend five quiet minutes alone today thinking about the life of the Prophet ﷺ, as 34:46 asks.

title: Look at the heavens, and remember your time may be near.
subtitle: Two things to look at: creation and your own deadline
then: Allah asks why people do not look at the kingdom of the heavens and earth and learn that their Maker has no equal. Ibn Kathir says they should also be warned that {trap}their lives may be near their end{/trap}. Then: {idea}in what message after this will they believe?{/idea}
now: You look up from your phone at a clear night sky, and for a second you feel very small. Then you remember the colleague who died at forty-two last spring. {idea}Both thoughts point the same way.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about faith when I am older.
new: Creation shows me Allah, and my unknown deadline tells me not to wait.
try: Tonight, step outside and look at the sky for one minute. Then make one decision you have been putting off.

title: Whom Allah leaves astray, no one else can guide.
subtitle: Wandering blindly in one's own excess

row.title: anyone else
sub: a guru, a trend, a feed

then: After asking what message people will believe if not this one, Allah says whoever He sends astray has no guide, and He leaves them {trap}wandering blindly in their transgression{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to 10:101: signs and warners do not benefit those who will not believe.
now: You try every self-help book, every podcast, every life coach, hoping one will finally fix you. {idea}None of them can guide a heart Allah has not opened.{/idea} Ask Him first, then the books can help.
old: The right expert or book will set me straight.
new: Guidance comes only from Allah, so I turn to Him before anyone else.
try: Before you look for advice on your next problem, make a short dua for guidance first.

title: When is the Hour? Only my Lord knows, and it comes suddenly.
subtitle: The question that matters is not when, but how ready
then: Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ when the Hour would come, mostly to mock it. He was told to say its knowledge is with Allah alone. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that {trap}the Hour will come while two men have spread a cloth to trade and cannot fold it, while a man raises food to his mouth and cannot eat it{/trap}.
now: You scroll videos about end-times signs, counting which ones have happened. Meanwhile your prayers are late and your mother is waiting for a call. {idea}The Hour comes suddenly, mid-errand.{/idea} Readiness is today's work.
old: If I knew when, I would prepare.
new: Not knowing when is the reason to be ready now.
try: Ask yourself: if it came during my next ordinary task, would I be at peace? Fix one thing.

title: If I knew the unseen, I would have avoided all harm.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say he does not know the future

row.title: no power
sub: over my own harm or benefit

row.title: no unseen
sub: or I would have avoided loss

row.title: Allah alone
sub: even the Prophet ﷺ said so

then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to say he has no power over benefit or harm to himself, except as Allah wills. Ibn 'Abbas explained: {idea}if I knew the unseen, I would know which deals would profit, and poverty would never touch me{/idea}. He is only a warner and a bringer of good news.
now: Someone offers to read your future in a cup, a palm, an app. You are anxious about the job interview, the test results. {idea}If even the Prophet ﷺ did not know the unseen, no one at a market stall does.{/idea}
old: Someone might be able to tell me what is coming.
new: The unseen is with Allah alone, so I trust Him and prepare.
try: When anxious about the future today, say: Allah knows and I do not, and do one practical thing.

title: Expecting a child, they both turned to Allah.
subtitle: Spouses made for rest, and a prayer for a good child
then: Allah created people from one soul and made its mate from it, so that each finds rest in the other. Ibn Kathir cites 30:21: {reward}He put between you affection and mercy{/reward}. As the pregnancy grows heavy, the couple both pray: if You give us a good child, {idea}we will be among the grateful{/idea}.
now: The ultrasound appointment. Both of you holding hands, saying ya Allah, let everything be okay. {idea}Fear brings couples to their knees together.{/idea} The promise you make there matters.
old: Once the baby is healthy, the worrying is over.
new: The gratitude I promise in fear is what Allah watches for after the gift.
try: If you have a spouse or child, thank Allah for them by name tonight, out loud.

title: When He gave the gift, they gave others the credit.
subtitle: Forgetting the Giver once the child arrives
then: When Allah gave them a good child, {trap}they ascribed partners to Him in what He gave{/trap}. Ibn Kathir prefers Al-Hasan's view: this is not about Adam and Hawwa', but about later people who did this. The verse moves from the first pair to humanity in general.
now: The baby is born healthy. Someone says it was the lucky bracelet, the special diet, the great hospital. The doctors deserve thanks. {idea}But the gift came from Allah.{/idea} The first thanks belongs to Him.
old: Things worked out because of what we did.
new: I thank people for their part, but the gift itself is from Allah alone.
try: Think of one answered prayer. Thank Allah for it first, then thank the people who helped.

title: They worship what creates nothing and was itself created.
subtitle: A simple test for anything you treat as ultimate
then: Allah asks how people can associate with Him things that create nothing and are themselves created. Ibn Kathir cites 22:73: {trap}all the false gods together could not create a fly{/trap}, and if a fly took something from them, they could not get it back.
now: Your career, your brand, your bank balance. You made them, or someone else did. {trap}None of them can create even a fly.{/trap} Yet some mornings they decide whether you feel worth anything.
old: What I have built is what gives my life meaning.
new: Only the Creator deserves my devotion, not anything created.
try: Watch a small insect for a minute today. Remember no human power could make it.

title: They cannot help their worshippers, or even themselves.
subtitle: The idol that could not defend itself
then: Ibn Kathir tells of 'Amr bin Al-Jamuh, whose idol two young Companions kept overturning at night. He left a sword by it and said: defend yourself. When it was found tied to a dead dog, he said: {trap}had you been a god, you would not end up like this{/trap}. He embraced Islam and was later martyred at Uhud.
now: You count on your contacts, your savings, your reputation to protect you. Then a rumor spreads, or the market drops, and they cannot even save themselves. {idea}Rely on what cannot fall.{/idea}
old: What I lean on will hold me up when trouble comes.
new: Anything that cannot protect itself cannot protect me.
try: Name the one thing you lean on most besides Allah. Say: Hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: Call them to guidance or stay silent, it is the same.
subtitle: The idols cannot hear or follow
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the idols do not hear those who call them, so calling them or ignoring them makes no difference. He cites Ibrahim's words to his father in 19:42: {trap}why do you worship what neither hears nor sees nor helps you at all?{/trap}
now: You pour your worries into a group chat, a diary, a playlist at 3am. Nothing answers back. {idea}Allah is As-Sami', the One who hears{/idea}, even what you have not said out loud.
old: Talking it out anywhere will make me feel better.
new: The One who truly hears is Allah, so I bring my worries to Him first.
try: Tonight, before telling anyone else about a worry, tell Allah in dua.

title: What you call on besides Allah are servants like you.
subtitle: Created things cannot answer prayer
then: Allah tells the idol worshippers that those they call on are servants like themselves. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}the worshipper is better than the idol{/idea}, for the worshipper at least hears, sees and has strength. The verse challenges them: call on them and let them answer.
now: You keep checking for a message from the one person you think can fix your situation: a manager, an ex, a relative with connections. {trap}They are servants like you{/trap}, as needy as you. {idea}Ask the One they all depend on.{/idea}
old: The right person can solve this for me.
new: People are servants like me, so I ask their Master first.
try: Before asking anyone for a big favor this week, ask Allah for it in two rak'ahs.

title: Do they have feet, hands, eyes or ears? Then plot, and wait.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ fearless challenge
then: The verse asks whether the idols have feet, hands, eyes or ears. Then the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: call your partners, plot against me, and {idea}give me no respite{/idea}. Ibn Kathir compares it to Hud's words in 11:54-56: {reward}I put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord{/reward}.
now: You are afraid of the evil eye, a curse, a superstition about the wrong day to travel. {idea}They have no hands to touch you without Allah's leave.{/idea} Say your adhkar and walk out the door with calm.
old: I need to be careful not to anger unseen powers.
new: Nothing harms me without Allah's permission, so I trust Him and stop fearing.
try: Say the morning adhkar today, then let go of one superstition you have been holding.

title: My protector is the One who sent the Book.
subtitle: The Prophet's answer to every threat
then: The idolaters were told to call on their so-called partners and plot against the Prophet ﷺ without delay. His answer: {reward}my protector is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He protects the righteous.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains: His support is enough for me, in this life and the next, {idea}and for every righteous believer after me.{/idea}
now: A rumor is going around the office about you. People with more influence seem to be against you. {trap}You feel small and outnumbered.{/trap} {reward}The One who sent the Quran is the ally of those who do right.{/reward}
old: I am safe only if the powerful people are on my side.
new: If I stay righteous, Allah is my protector, and that is enough.
